### Security
- Addresses CVE-2026-121885, untrusted image labels could be used to trick podman auto-update into restarting incorrect systemd units [GHSA-55rm-rwr7-q2wr](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/security/advisories/GHSA-55rm-rwr7-q2wr).
- Addresses CVE-2026-111361, malicious containers images could be able to bypass Digest and Signature validation [GHSA-pggw-qqjf-6cxw](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/container-libs/security/advisories/GHSA-pggw-qqjf-6cxw).
- Addresses CVE-2026-123876, default seccomp profile socket deny rule could be bypass by a malicious container.

### Features
- The `podman push` command now supports a new option, `--platform`, which selects and pushes a single platform-specific manifest instead of the entire list.
- The `podman kube play` command now supports a new option, `--validate`, which determines how unrecognized YAML fields are handled ([#18332](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/18332)).
- The `podman kube play` command now supports a new option, `--label`, to set labels on created containers, pods, volumes, and secrets ([#26450](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/26450)).
- The `podman kube play` command can now create multiple pods if more than 1 replica is requested by a deployment using the new `--multiple-pods` option ([#26769](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/26769)).
- The `podman kube play --build` command now supports building images from subdirectories of the main context directory ([#28148](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/28418)).
- Quadlet `.container` files now support a new key, `Umask`, to set the default umask for the created container ([#25278](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/25278)).
- All Quadlet files now support a new key, `SetMountsDependency`, configuring whether the generated unit will use `RequiresMountsFor`, `WantsMountsFor`, or no dependency at all on required source paths ([#29946](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29946)).
- The `podman farm list` command now supports two new options, `--quiet`, which will print only the names of active farms, and `--noheading`, which omits column headers from the output.
- The `podman artifact ls` command now supports two new options, `--format=json`, which will output machine-readable JSON, and `--quiet`, which prints only artifact digests.
- The `podman create` command now supports a new option, `--passwd`, to add entries to `/etc/passwd` in the container (this has previously been available with `podman run`).
- The `podman info` command now includes detailed information on the features supported by OCI runtimes.
- The `podman events --filter` command now supports a new filter, `network=`, to filter to events pertaining to a specific network ([#29387](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29387)).
- The `podman auto-update` command has been enabled on the remote Podman client.
- The `StartInterval` field in image healthcheck configuration is now respected, allowing images to configure startup healthchecks ([#27724](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/27724)).
- The `podman image scp` command now supports two new options, `--compression-format` and `--compression-level`, to compress data during transfer ([#23192](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/23192)).
- The `podman auto-update` command now supports a new option, `--filter`, to selectively update only containers that match the given filters.
- The `podman ps --sort` command now allows sorting by pod.
- The `podman ps --filter` command now supports a new filter, `status!`, which matches containers not in the given state ([#21398](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/21398)).

### Changes
- Podman now requires Go v1.26 or higher to build.
- The Podman machine WSL provider now has native systemd support, existing machines continue to be supported for now with our old custom systemd setup. We require at least WSL version 2.5.1 now, although we recommend using at least 2.7.5 for proper nftables networking support.
- The `podman kube play` command now uses the `securityContext.seccompProfile` fields in Kubernetes YAML for Seccomp configuration. Support for the existing annotation-based configuration of Seccomp is now deprecated, and will be removed with Podman 7.0.
- The `podman inspect` command on containers now includes three new fields, `DNSNames` (containing all names the container can be accessed via), `IsInitCtr` (whether the container is an init container), and `InitContainerType` (what type of init container this is, if it is one) ([#29811](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29811)).
- The `podman inspect` command on containers now only includes user-added DNS aliases in the `Aliases` field, which previously displayed all DNS aliases, improving Docker compatibility.
- The `podman inspect` command on containers now properly populates the `ConsoleSize` field for running containers ([#28368](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/28368)).
- Systemd units created by Podman healthchecks are now named much more clearly (`libpod-healthcheck-$CONTAINERID-$randsuffix.service`) ([#29373](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29373)).
- Signal proxying is now enabled for attached `podman exec` commands. As such, killing a `podman exec` command with Control-C or similar should now also kill the processes started in the container (similar to how `podman run` already works) ([#19486](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/19486)).
- The deprecated `--cpu-rt-period` and `--cpu-rt-runtime` options for `podman create`, `podman run`, `podman update`, and `podman container clone` are now hidden and undocumented. They have not been functional since the removal of cgroups v1 support and will be removed entirely in Podman v7.

## Added

- [#6393](https://github.com/firecracker-microvm/firecracker/pull/6393): Added  support for Nitro Sandboxes. Firecracker can now launch and manage isolated VMs that the Nitro Hypervisor carves out of the parent EC2 instance, as an alternative to KVM. Firecracker drives the Nitro Enclaves driver (`/dev/nitro_enclaves`) instead of `/dev/kvm`, and keeps its existing API, jailer and virtio device model. A sandbox is configured with the new `PUT /enclave` API, in confidential or direct mode. See the [Nitro Sandboxes documentation](https://github.com/firecracker-microvm/firecracker/blob/firecracker-v1.18/docs/nitro-sandboxes/README.md).

### ⚠️ Upgrade notes

* **Custom login UIs:** completing or failing an OIDC or SAML request (`CreateCallback`, `CreateResponse`) now requires the `session.link` permission, whatever headers are sent. The hosted Login V2 and custom login UIs whose service user has the `IAM_LOGIN_CLIENT` role are not affected. If yours uses another user, for example an `IAM_OWNER` personal access token, grant it `IAM_LOGIN_CLIENT` **before upgrading**.
* **Local authentication disabled:** password checks through the Session API now follow the login policy of the user's organization, like Login V1. Users of an organization that disables username/password login can no longer sign in or change their password with a password. Send them to their identity provider.
* **Public host header:** the `x-zitadel-public-host` header must be a single plain host with an optional port. Other values are now rejected instead of ignored.
* **Notification links:** if the host that triggered a notification is not valid, its links use the instance's primary domain. This includes notifications queued before the upgrade.
* **Login V1 authorization codes:** codes issued but not yet redeemed before the upgrade are rejected once. Affected users sign in again.
* **Login V2:**
  * External IdP sign-ins must be completed in the browser that started them. Sign-ins in progress during the upgrade have to be restarted.
  * Adding OTP email or SMS as a second factor now needs a confirmation click.
  * New texts were added. Custom login texts show the default for them until customized.
  * Custom builds: internal modules moved to `src/lib/server/` and `src/lib/actions/`, and the build fails on Server Actions missing from `checks/server-actions.allowlist.json`.

### Error changes

No existing error IDs, message keys or gRPC codes were changed or removed. The following calls can now return errors where they previously succeeded:

| Call | Condition | Error |
|---|---|---|
| `CreateCallback`, `CreateResponse` (OIDC/SAML) | caller lacks `session.link` | `PERMISSION_DENIED` |
| Session API password check | organization disables username/password login | `FAILED_PRECONDITION`, `Errors.Org.LoginPolicy.UsernamePasswordNotAllowed` |
| Session API password check | organization's login policy can't be read | `FAILED_PRECONDITION`, `Errors.Org.LoginPolicy.NotFound` |
| Session API password check | session has no user organization | `FAILED_PRECONDITION`, `Errors.User.UserIDMissing` (new, `COMMAND-Vz4tb`) |
| `/oauth/v2/token` (code issued through Login V1) | user not authenticated, or a different user than at issuance | `invalid_grant` |
| any request | invalid `x-zitadel-public-host` header | HTTP `400`, `invalid public host` (new, `HTTP-Rk7pX`) |

## Security

This release fixes the following security advisories (credit to the reporters named):

**High**
- [GHSA-wp3p-45h3-2v82](https://github.com/pi-hole/pi-hole/security/advisories/GHSA-wp3p-45h3-2v82) (CVSS 7.3): `pihole -r` and `pihole -up` still followed symlinks in `/etc/pihole` when writing `install.log`, `migration_backup_v6` and `hosts/custom.list`, so a `pihole` user could get root to take over files of their choice. Found by @cerodah, reported by @pmagayon.
- [GHSA-5w4v-f65m-323f](https://github.com/pi-hole/pi-hole/security/advisories/GHSA-5w4v-f65m-323f) (CVSS 7.3): root followed symlinks and config-supplied paths during the `macvendor.db` download, `pihole checkout` and `pihole uninstall`. Reported by @pmagayon.
- [GHSA-jvg9-fm8x-2jqq](https://github.com/pi-hole/pi-hole/security/advisories/GHSA-jvg9-fm8x-2jqq) (CVSS 7.3): `pihole -d` followed symlinks in `pihole`-owned directories, so root copied arbitrary files into the debug log and overwrote or re-owned others. Found by @wyx98765, reported by @pmagayon.
- [GHSA-cq9w-mv93-mxh7](https://github.com/pi-hole/pi-hole/security/advisories/GHSA-cq9w-mv93-mxh7) (CVSS 7.2): `gravity.sh` spliced `files.gravity` unescaped into SQL, which let an admin run commands as `pihole`. Core counterpart of FTL [GHSA-pj9m-9623-2g75](https://github.com/pi-hole/FTL/security/advisories/GHSA-pj9m-9623-2g75), which carries the CVE. Found by @Pedromdsn.

**Medium**
- [GHSA-qfq3-88xg-765w](https://github.com/pi-hole/pi-hole/security/advisories/GHSA-qfq3-88xg-765w) (CVSS 5.3): the `pihole -d` debug log, and so a tricorder upload, included the web password hash, the app password hash and the TOTP secret. Reported by @pmagayon.

## What's Changed

- Drop from root to the `pihole` user with `setpriv` instead of `sudo`, so `sudo` is no longer required (#6752).
- The installer no longer writes into `/etc/pihole` as root. `install.log`, the v6 migration backup, `hosts/custom.list` and `macvendor.db` are written as `pihole`.
- `pihole checkout` writes `ftlbranch` as `pihole`. `pihole uninstall` only removes the web interface directory if it is the official checkout, and removes the configured databases as `pihole`.
- `pihole -d` does its work in `pihole`-owned directories as `pihole`, and leaves password hashes and the TOTP secret out of the debug log.
- `gravity.sh` escapes a custom `files.gravity` before using it in SQL.
- Rely on the system's daily logrotate instead of Pi-hole's own nightly forced run, which collided with it and rotated the logs twice (#6749).
- Fix `pihole flush quiet` still printing, and `pihole flush once` not finishing its status line (#6698).
- Fix `pihole updatechecker` writing `null` remote hashes to `/etc/pihole/versions` when run from `/root` (#6735).
- Warn when a local repository is not marked as safe for git, instead of `pihole -v` silently showing the version as N/A (#6746).
- Sample 1000 rows per index for `ANALYZE` (#6748).
- Mark Quad9's unfiltered upstream as validating DNSSEC (#6740).
- Expect no sample of non-domain entries for a local list (#6728).
- Remove the unneeded `CAP_IPC_LOCK` (#6726).
- Tests: add Fedora 45 (#6753) and allow running the test suite with podman (#6754).

## Enhancements

* [#23470](https://github.com/netbox-community/netbox/issues/23470) - Add 3C8P, 3C12P, and 4C12P trunk cable profiles

## Performance Improvements

* [#23505](https://github.com/netbox-community/netbox/issues/23505) - Avoid redundant query conditions when filtering by a non-unique name or slug, such as MAC addresses by `interface` or device components by `device`
* [#23562](https://github.com/netbox-community/netbox/issues/23562) - Batch the loading of related objects read by export templates, rather than querying them for each object
* [#23563](https://github.com/netbox-community/netbox/issues/23563) - Batch the loading of related objects when rendering global search results
* [#23564](https://github.com/netbox-community/netbox/issues/23564) - Batch the loading of cable terminations and their parent objects when listing cables, cable terminations, ports, and power feeds via the REST API
* [#23565](https://github.com/netbox-community/netbox/issues/23565) - Batch the loading of deferred fields and related objects which the GraphQL query optimizer can't anticipate, such as those read when resolving `link_peers` and `connected_endpoints`

## Bug Fixes

* [#23185](https://github.com/netbox-community/netbox/issues/23185) - Prevent the deletion of a region or site group from also deleting the circuit terminations attached to its sites and locations
* [#23260](https://github.com/netbox-community/netbox/issues/23260) - Fix exception when applying migration `dcim.0245_consolidate_unique_constraints` on installations whose location, region, or site group unique constraints have auto-generated names
* [#23407](https://github.com/netbox-community/netbox/issues/23407) - Restrict the image attachments listed under an object's Images tab to those the user is permitted to view
* [#23446](https://github.com/netbox-community/netbox/issues/23446) - Prevent duplicate submissions of object add and edit forms (such as duplicate image attachments) by disabling the submit button after the first click
* [#23447](https://github.com/netbox-community/netbox/issues/23447) - Fix exception when ordering REST API results by an object count field (e.g. `count_ipaddresses`) which is omitted from the response by `brief` or `fields`
* [#23477](https://github.com/netbox-community/netbox/issues/23477) - Include the `asn_count` field in the REST API representation of ASN ranges
* [#23478](https://github.com/netbox-community/netbox/issues/23478) - Validate `{module}` placeholders in component labels and module bay templates when installing a module, rather than raising an exception or resolving them to an empty string
* [#23486](https://github.com/netbox-community/netbox/issues/23486) - Record pre-change data in the change log for virtual chassis members when creating, editing, or deleting a virtual chassis
* [#23510](https://github.com/netbox-community/netbox/issues/23510) - Prevent a queued background job from running after it has been deleted or marked as failed
* [#23511](https://github.com/netbox-community/netbox/issues/23511) - Display the correct file path on a script's Source tab, and identify the script file (rather than `<string>`) in error tracebacks
* [#23534](https://github.com/netbox-community/netbox/issues/23534) - Fix `IntegrityError` exception when completing a job whose owner already has a notification for it
* [#23535](https://github.com/netbox-community/netbox/issues/23535) - Prevent a duplicate recurring sync job from being created when a data source is saved as its scheduled sync finishes
* [#23542](https://github.com/netbox-community/netbox/issues/23542) - Fix `FileNotFoundError` exception when synchronizing a local data source whose subdirectory paths repeat the root path (e.g. `/scripts/scripts_old/`)
* [#23558](https://github.com/netbox-community/netbox/issues/23558) - Fix errors when editing an API token without permission to view users, or from the user's own API tokens view
* [#23559](https://github.com/netbox-community/netbox/issues/23559) - Fix the prefetching of related objects shown as display attributes in global search results
* [#23574](https://github.com/netbox-community/netbox/issues/23574) - Fix exception when passing `null` to several filters (e.g. `present_in_vrf_id`, `available_at_site`, and `interface_id`), and support filtering data sources by `sync_interval=null`
* [#23584](https://github.com/netbox-community/netbox/issues/23584) - Enforce SSO allowlist settings (e.g. `WHITELISTED_DOMAINS` and `WHITELISTED_EMAILS`) by adding `auth_allowed` to the default `SOCIAL_AUTH_PIPELINE`
* [#23585](https://github.com/netbox-community/netbox/issues/23585) - Enforce view permissions on parent and related objects when adding individual components or component templates, and when bulk adding prefixes, IP addresses, and VLANs
* [#23595](https://github.com/netbox-community/netbox/issues/23595) - Implement `update_dependent_objects()` for wireless links, circuit terminations, and channel subinterfaces, to rebuild cable paths after writes which bypass `save()`
* [#23596](https://github.com/netbox-community/netbox/issues/23596) - Record pre-change data in the change log for components adopted when installing a module
* [#23597](https://github.com/netbox-community/netbox/issues/23597) - Record change log entries and trigger event rules for port mappings created from device type and module type templates, or moved with a module to another device

## v3.2.9 (2026-11-09)

### Breaking Changes in v3.2.9

- [#9741](https://github.com/nautobot/nautobot/issues/9741) - Due to updating `social-auth-core` and `social-auth-app-django`, deployments that override the `SOCIAL_AUTH_PIPELINE` setting may need to update their configuration to add an entry for `"social_core.pipeline.social_auth.social_names"`. If this is not added, some SSO backends may no longer automatically populate the `first_name` and `last_name` fields when creating new User records in Nautobot.

### Security in v3.2.9

- [GHSA-h3qx-qrj8-q6wf](https://github.com/nautobot/nautobot/security/advisories/GHSA-h3qx-qrj8-q6wf) - Fixed a vulnerability in which the "Export Object List" system Job, and any other code that applied object permissions to API tokens, allowed a user to read the keys of other users' API tokens. Applying object permissions to tokens now always limits every user, including superusers, to their own tokens; staff users with the appropriate permissions can still manage all users' tokens in the Django admin interface.
- [GHSA-h3qx-qrj8-q6wf](https://github.com/nautobot/nautobot/security/advisories/GHSA-h3qx-qrj8-q6wf) - Changed the "Export Object List" and "Import Objects" system Jobs to refuse to export or import API tokens, as doing so would write token keys to a file that other users may be able to download.
- [GHSA-546w-cg72-vf5w](https://github.com/nautobot/nautobot/security/advisories/GHSA-546w-cg72-vf5w) - Fixed a bypass of the `sensitive_fields` control where a user-authored Jinja2 template could infer a sensitive field's value by filtering a queryset on it.
- [GHSA-w2v9-g37h-x98j](https://github.com/nautobot/nautobot/security/advisories/GHSA-w2v9-g37h-x98j) - Fixed a bypass of the `sensitive_fields` control where the `hyperlinked_object` and `hyperlinked_object_target_new_tab` template filters could read a sensitive field or private attribute of an object.
- [GHSA-w2v9-g37h-x98j](https://github.com/nautobot/nautobot/security/advisories/GHSA-w2v9-g37h-x98j) - Fixed a bypass of the `sensitive_fields` control where a user-authored Jinja2 template could read a sensitive field through a model or field method that reads a field by name, such as `serializable_value()`.
- [#9716](https://github.com/nautobot/nautobot/issues/9716) - Fixed the "Non-Racked Devices" table on the Rack detail view displaying devices that the user did not have permission to view.
- [#9741](https://github.com/nautobot/nautobot/issues/9741) - Updated dependency `social-auth-core` to `>=6.2.0,<6.3` to mitigate CVE-2026-115910.
- [#9751](https://github.com/nautobot/nautobot/issues/9751) - Fixed the circuit "Swap Terminations" view not enforcing the `circuits.change_circuittermination` permission or object-level permission constraints on the circuit terminations being modified.
- [#9764](https://github.com/nautobot/nautobot/issues/9764) - Updated dependency `django` to `>=5.2.19,<5.3` to mitigate multiple security vulnerabilities.
- [#9765](https://github.com/nautobot/nautobot/issues/9765) - Updated dependency `oauthlib` to 4.0.1 to mitigate CVE-2026-49272. As this is not a direct dependency, it will not auto-update when upgrading. Please be sure to upgrade your local environment.

### Added in v3.2.9

- [#9714](https://github.com/nautobot/nautobot/issues/9714) - Added the `PERSISTENT_CACHE_TIMEOUT` setting to optionally expire custom field, relationship, and similar caches that are otherwise only refreshed when their underlying data changes.

### Changed in v3.2.9

- [GHSA-w2v9-g37h-x98j](https://github.com/nautobot/nautobot/security/advisories/GHSA-w2v9-g37h-x98j) - Changed the `meta` filter in Jinja2 templates to return only the attributes that identify a model, such as `app_label` and `verbose_name`; any other `_meta` attribute now raises an error.
- [#9762](https://github.com/nautobot/nautobot/issues/9762) - Updated Marketplace entries for Apps no longer relevant in 3.2.

### Removed in v3.2.9

- [#9676](https://github.com/nautobot/nautobot/issues/9676) - Removed support for `--database` parameter from `nautobot-server generate_test_data` command, as it did not generally work correctly for non-default databases.

### Fixed in v3.2.9

- [#6475](https://github.com/nautobot/nautobot/issues/6475) - Fixed custom fields, relationships, and notes not being available when assigning an existing contact or team to an object.

# QuestDB 10.2.0

QuestDB 10.2.0 adds `GROUPING SETS`, `ROLLUP` and `CUBE`, row-level retention for materialized views, a `DEDUP SKIP` mode that keeps the first-written row, and opt-in power-loss durability for WAL tables, enabled with `cairo.commit.mode=adaptive`. QWP ingestion of small messages is much faster, and this release fixes a large batch of wrong-result, crash and hang bugs in queries, out-of-order ingestion and Parquet partitions.

This release contains **a few breaking changes**. Read the [Breaking changes](#breaking-changes-boom) section before you upgrade, especially if you create materialized views with `LIMIT` or window functions, send the designated timestamp twice over QWP, or may need to downgrade after using `DEDUP SKIP`.

For any questions or feedback, please join us on [Slack](https://slack.questdb.com/) or on [Discourse](https://community.questdb.com/).

See also our _prettier_ [release notes](https://questdb.com/release-notes/) page.

## Breaking changes :boom:

- **`CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW` rejects `LIMIT` in queries that read the base table, and base-table window functions nested in expressions or `SAMPLE BY` subqueries.** Replaying older `SHOW CREATE` output that contains them fails. [#7263](https://github.com/questdb/questdb/pull/7263)
- **QWP rejects table blocks that carry the designated timestamp twice**, once through `at(...)` and once as a named column. Before this change, QuestDB accepted them and stored wrong timestamps. A sender that uses both forms on one table now gets a schema error on every later batch for that table. [#8052](https://github.com/questdb/questdb/pull/8052)
- **An unknown `cairo.commit.mode` value now fails startup**, instead of silently selecting `nosync`. [#7411](https://github.com/questdb/questdb/pull/7411)
- **After 10.2.0 has run on a database, downgrading, writing with the older version and upgrading again is not supported.** See [downgrade to an earlier release](https://questdb.com/docs/concepts/durability/#downgrade). [#7411](https://github.com/questdb/questdb/pull/7411)
- **Downgrading after using `DEDUP SKIP`:** older versions treat `SKIP` tables as `UPSERT` without an error, and suspend WAL apply when they replay a logged `ALTER TABLE ... DEDUP SKIP`. [#7885](https://github.com/questdb/questdb/pull/7885)

## Highlights

### `GROUPING SETS`, `ROLLUP` and `CUBE`

`GROUP BY` and `SAMPLE BY` now accept `ROLLUP`, `CUBE` and `GROUPING SETS`, with the `GROUPING()` and `GROUPING_ID()` functions. One query returns subtotals and a grand total in a single scan of the input:

```sql
SELECT symbol, side, sum(amount)
FROM trades
GROUP BY ROLLUP(symbol, side);
```

Grouping sets run in parallel where the plan allows. `SAMPLE BY` grouping sets support `FILL` with `NULL`, constants or `NONE`. `cairo.sql.max.grouping.sets` caps how many grouping sets one query expands to (default 4096). Grouping sets do not vectorize: they ran 1.4x slower than the equivalent `UNION ALL` of plain `GROUP BY`s serially, and up to 6.9x slower in parallel, in the PR's benchmark. [#6853](https://github.com/questdb/questdb/pull/6853)

### Passthrough views and row-level retention

Materialized views can now be passthrough views: a filtered copy of a table (`SELECT ... WHERE`, no `SAMPLE BY`), kept up to date as rows arrive. The new `EXPIRE ROWS` policy adds row-level retention on top, and hides expired rows of a materialized view from every query: `WHEN <predicate>`, `KEEP LATEST`, `KEEP [N] HIGHEST|LOWEST`, or a window predicate. For monotonic `WHEN` policies, such as `ts < now()`, a background job also frees the disk; `cairo.mat.view.row.expiry.cleanup.*` settings control it. `ALTER MATERIALIZED VIEW ... SET EXPIRE ROWS` and `... DROP EXPIRE` change a view's policy. [#7263](https://github.com/questdb/questdb/pull/7263)

### `DEDUP SKIP`: keep the first row

The new `DEDUP SKIP` mode keeps the first-written row and drops later duplicates, where `UPSERT` keeps the last one. `CREATE TABLE`, CTAS and `ALTER TABLE ... DEDUP` accept it, and `SHOW CREATE TABLE` prints it. Commits that hold only duplicates leave native and Parquet partitions untouched, and resending unchanged rows into `DEDUP UPSERT` Parquet partitions no longer rewrites them. [#7885](https://github.com/questdb/questdb/pull/7885)

### Power-loss durability for WAL tables (opt-in)

`cairo.commit.mode=adaptive` makes WAL tables survive power loss for much less than `sync` mode costs. QuestDB flushes the WAL on commit, applies it to table files without per-apply flushes, and rebuilds the table files from the WAL after a crash, so the server restarts with consistent tables instead of failing on a damaged partition. `cairo.adaptive.commit.group.window` (default 50 ms) batches flushes across commits, so commits acknowledged within the last window can be lost. Pair it with `request_durable_ack=local` on QWP clients (`local,replicated` on QuestDB Enterprise) to be told when each batch is on disk, or set the window to `0`. The default stays `nosync`. [#7411](https://github.com/questdb/questdb/pull/7411)

Release v4.0.1

The third release candidate of TerminusDB 12.1 hardens the indexing and commit pipeline, finalises the storage layout and embedded vectorlink startup, and makes raw JSON documents read back exactly as they were written. The small delta of insights from formal ACID testing with ALICE and Jepsen tools were incorporated.

Additionally, this release candidate is now also the fastest TerminusDB release ever, with further performance improvements along the 12.1 release candidates series. WOQL up to 60% faster, serial inserts up to 2x faster, parallel inserts up to 50x faster for parallel workloads compared to pre-12.1 levels.

Simply the best TerminusDB ever.

Headline changes:

* Atomic commit application guarded by compare-and-swap (CAS), requests held until startup components are ready, and a formal ACID test suite guarding the invariants
* Multi-process indexer handoff so embedding indexing no longer starves ordinary requests, and the global atom-GC stall that followed large index runs is gone
* Verbatim `sys:JSONDocument` (vanilla JSON) reads by default across every instance selector — **breaking, intentional:** clients relying on the injected `@id` must pass `raw_id=true` (see Behavior changes)
* `TERMINUSDB_STORE` storage root, a new `~/.terminusdb` default layout, opt-in embedded vectorlink, and serve startup failures that exit non-zero
* Real HTTP statuses for streaming document formats instead of a blanket 200
* GraphQL subclass interfaces (example: `... on MyClass { field }`)
* Type inference ladder: a specificity staircase for ambiguous candidates (precise and fast type resolution)
* Idempotent `merge_repeats` resubmission and unbound-prefix errors that name the fix
* `xdd:dateTimeInterval` single instants and full-day dates, and `xsd:duration` beyond 255 days
* Document inserts even faster after a commit-path profiling pass — ~7% on serial inserts, up to ~10% on wide documents

Storage layout and vectorlink configuration changes:

* **`TERMINUSDB_STORE` is the new official storage variable.** It names the storage root; the database lives at `<root>/db` and the embedded vectorlink index at `<root>/vectorlink`. The `terminusdb serve --store` flag now sets `TERMINUSDB_STORE`. `TERMINUSDB_SERVER_DB_PATH` remains valid as a legacy override naming the db dir directly — when both are set, `DB_PATH` wins for the database and `STORE` still informs vectorlink.
* **New default storage layout.** Without configuration, the store resolves to `~/.terminusdb/db` instead of the cwd-relative `./storage/db`. **Migration:** move an existing default local store into the new layout (`~/.terminusdb/` contents → `~/.terminusdb/db/`, keeping `../vectorlink/` as a db sibling), or keep `TERMINUSDB_SERVER_DB_PATH` pointing at the old location. Default Docker users are unaffected — the image now exports `TERMINUSDB_STORE`, so databases remain in their existing location.
* **Embedded vectorlink is opt-in.** The engine starts only when `TERMINUSDB_STORE` (or `serve --store`) or `VECTORLINK_DATA_DIR` is set; otherwise it logs a notice and stays disabled. A `TERMINUSDB_SERVER_DB_PATH`-only install that wants vectorlink must set `TERMINUSDB_STORE` or `VECTORLINK_DATA_DIR`.
* **Concurrent vectorlink instances degrade to read-only.** When the embed-cache lock is held by another process, the second instance disables the cache, skips startup cleanup, refuses all index writes, and serves search queries only — reported on the console.
* **Startup failures exit non-zero.** A port already in use (or any other serve startup failure) now reports the real error and exits 1 instead of printing command help and exiting 0. Also cleaned up boot messages.

## New functionality

* Atomic commit CAS, startup readiness, and a formal ACID suite [#2639](https://github.com/terminusdb/terminusdb/pull/2639)
* Multi process indexer handoff [#2644](https://github.com/terminusdb/terminusdb/pull/2644) [#2651](https://github.com/terminusdb/terminusdb/pull/2651)
* `xdd:dateTimeInterval`: single instants and full-day dates [#2629](https://github.com/terminusdb/terminusdb/pull/2629)
* CLI startup: `TERMINUSDB_STORE` storage root, embedded vectorlink resolution, loud serve failures [#2630](https://github.com/terminusdb/terminusdb/pull/2630)
* Type inference ladder: specificity staircase for ambiguous candidates [#2638](https://github.com/terminusdb/terminusdb/pull/2638)
* GraphQL subclass interfaces [#2647](https://github.com/terminusdb/terminusdb/pull/2647)

## Behavior changes

* **`sys:JSONDocument` reads are verbatim by default.** `raw_id` on the document API now defaults to `false`: raw JSON documents read back as submitted, `@`-prefixed members like `"@type"` and nested `"@id"` included — they are document content, not annotations (key order and whitespace canonicalize). Applies across every instance selector (`id`, `ids`, `type`, `id_prefix`, `query`, bare listing) in single-document and `as_list` output. `identifiers=false` no longer strips `@`-members from raw documents, and field names URI-escaped at insert now decode correctly on read. **Migration:** pass `raw_id=true` to keep the injected `@id`; no data migration is needed.
* `xdd:dateTimeInterval` keeps a single instant a single instant: a bare dateTime literal reads back as supplied — with `Z`, an offset, or zoneless — instead of a zero-length `T/T` pair, distinguished by a new `point` flag in the lexical entry (an explicit pair still renders `T/T`). A bare ISO date denotes the whole day `[D, D+1)` (`P1D`), the same interval as `D/D`. Date pairs round-trip verbatim: `2025-01-01/2025-03-31` reads back unchanged, dates inclusive, and zoneless datetimes render as local time rather than acquiring `Z`. Filter equality treats every spelling of the same period as equal, the supported range is increased, and values stored before this change are unaffected [#2626](https://github.com/terminusdb/terminusdb/issues/2626)
* `xsd:duration` now supports > 255

## [v1.156.0](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/releases/tag/v1.156.0)

Released at 2026-11-09

* FEATURE: all VictoriaMetrics [Enterprise](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/enterprise/) components: run with the `-eula` command-line flag to accept [ESA](https://victoriametrics.com/legal/esa/). License keys are no longer verified. The `-license`, `-licenseFile`, `-licenseFile.reloadInterval` and `-license.forceOffline` flags are deprecated and are treated as `-eula`, so existing setups keep working. See [Running VictoriaMetrics Enterprise](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/enterprise/#running-victoriametrics-enterprise).
* FEATURE: all VictoriaMetrics components: add new metric `process_cgroup_cpu_throttled_seconds_total` which exposes CPU throttling. See [#10430](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/issues/10430).
* FEATURE: [vmagent](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/vmagent/) and [Single-node VictoriaMetrics](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/single-server-victoriametrics/): support `authentication_method: WorkloadIdentity` in [azure_sd_configs](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/sd_configs/#azure_sd_configs). It allows discovering Azure VMs from Kubernetes clusters with [workload identity federation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/workload-id/workload-identity-federation) without a static client secret. See [#11558](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/issues/11558). Thanks to @banlor for contribution.
* FEATURE: [vmagent](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/vmagent/): add a new flag `-remoteWrite.queuePath`, which allows configuring [persistent-queue](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/vmagent/#on-disk-persistence) path for each `-remoteWrite.url` independently. See [#11662](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/issues/11662).
* FEATURE: [vmagent](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/vmagent/): add `vmagent_kafka_consumer_rebalance_events_total` and `vmagent_kafka_consumer_assigned_partitions` metrics for monitoring partition rebalancing and distribution. See [partition distribution](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/integrations/kafka/#partition-distribution) and [#11370](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/issues/11370).
* FEATURE: [vmalert](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/vmalert/): add `-notifier.sanitizeLabelNames` command-line flag. Set it to `false` to send alert label names to notifiers without replacing characters outside `[a-zA-Z0-9_:]` with underscores. This is useful for Alertmanager v0.27.0 or newer, which [supports UTF-8 label names](https://prometheus.io/docs/alerting/latest/configuration/#utf-8-strict-mode) when not running in classic mode. See [#11629](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/issues/11629).
* FEATURE: [vmsingle](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/single-server-victoriametrics/), `vmstorage` and `vmselect` in [VictoriaMetrics cluster](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/cluster-victoriametrics/): expose the working-set cache mode via `vm_cache_mode` for `storage/tsid`, `storage/metricIDs`, `storage/metricName`, `indexdb/tagFiltersLoops`, and `promql/rollupResult` cache. Values are `0` for split, `1` for switching, and `2` for whole. This metric helps users understand the internal memory and cache mechanisms. See [#11860](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/issues/11860).

* BUGFIX: all VictoriaMetrics components: OS `solaris` fixes compilation error. See [#11850](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/pull/11850). Thanks to @szaydel for contribution.
* BUGFIX: all VictoriaMetrics components: correctly detect `CPU` and `memory` `cgroup` limits configured via [systemd slices](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd.slice.html) in `cgroup v1`. Previously, only the global host cgroup limit was used, which could cause OOM errors and CPU throttling. See [#11827](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/issues/11827).
* BUGFIX: [alerts](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/blob/master/deployment/docker/rules): stop [vmbackupmanager alerting rules](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/blob/master/deployment/docker/rules/alerts-vmbackupmanager.yml) `NoLatestBackupWithinLastDay`, `NoHourlyBackupWithinLastDay`, `NoDailyBackupWithinLast3Days`, `NoWeeklyBackupWithinLast14Days` and `NoMonthlyBackupWithinLast62Days` from firing when scheduled backups are disabled via `-disableScheduledBackups` or the corresponding backup type is disabled via `-disableHourly`, `-disableDaily`, `-disableWeekly` or `-disableMonthly`. See [#11543](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/issues/11543).
* BUGFIX: [stream aggregation](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/stream-aggregation/): properly delay flushes after a sudden ingestion lag spike when [aggregation windows](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/stream-aggregation/#aggregation-windows) are enabled. Previously, a data gap or a restart could reduce the tolerance for delayed samples to the aggregation interval, resulting in more dropped samples than necessary. See [#11866](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/pull/11866).
* BUGFIX: [stream aggregation](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/stream-aggregation/): prevent skipping aggregation and deduplication flushes when [aggregation windows](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/stream-aggregation/#aggregation-windows) are enabled and incoming samples are delayed by one interval or more, e.g. when the ingestion pipeline is overloaded. Previously, the flush delay could grow with the sample lag, causing skipped flushes and gaps in the results. Now the flush delay is capped at 90% of the aggregation or deduplication interval. # Changelog

## 3.2.5

### Grafana Mimir

* [CHANGE] Alertmanager: Enforce that SNS receivers provide explicit credentials (access key and secret key) by default. This prevents malicious users from creating a SNS receiver with a custom URL that then receives the Alertmanager's AWS credentials. The existing behaviour can be restored by setting `-alertmanager.require-explicit-sns-credentials=false`. #17320
* [CHANGE] Alertmanager: Reject SNS receivers that set `use_aws_http_client`. The AWS SDK HTTP client does not use the Alertmanager receivers firewall, so this setting could be used to reach addresses blocked by `-alertmanager.receivers-firewall-block-private-addresses` or `-alertmanager.receivers-firewall-block-cidr-networks`. #17320
* [CHANGE] Alertmanager: Enforce restrictions on tenant configuration when loading configuration from storage, not just when receiving it via API. This ensures that new restrictions introduced cannot be circumvented by existing config. Existing tenants' configuration that fails validation can be exempted from this restriction with `-alertmanager.tenants-exempt-from-config-validation-for-existing-config`. #17320

MISP 2.5.51 is a maintenance/hot-fix release focused on dependency updates, removing obsolete development components, and keeping the codebase clean and maintainable.

### Improvements and Changes

- **OTP Library Update**
  - Upgraded `otphp` from `^10.0` to `^11.5`, aligning with the dependency version used in the development branch.

- **Removal of Legacy DebugKit Dependency**
  - Removed the unused CakePHP DebugKit development dependency.
  - The legacy CakePHP 2 DebugKit has not been updated since 2018, and its debugging toolbar was never enabled in MISP.
  - Avoids introducing unnecessary dependencies from newer DebugKit versions targeting CakePHP 3+.

- **Docker and Overmind Cleanup**
  - Updated Overmind dependency hints to remove references to DebugKit.
  - Newly built Docker images no longer include this obsolete development dependency.

### Upgrade Recommendation

Users are encouraged to upgrade to **MISP 2.5.51** to benefit from the updated dependencies and maintenance improvements.

This release does not introduce new user-facing functionality but contributes to maintaining a cleaner and more sustainable MISP codebase.

Passbolt 5.18.0 "Superstylin" introduces custom themes to personalize your workspace, expands Quick Access support to Secure Notes and Custom Fields, and enhances autofill reliability. This release also drives performance improvements on sharing operations, updates dependencies, and brings in essential security fixes.

## Themes

The 5.18 release adds two new custom theme options, Sakura and Layette, providing enhanced personalization for the user's workspace appearance.

These themes allow users to adapt the interface to their personal preferences while maintaining consistent user experience throughout the application.

If you have an idea for a new theme let us know on the [Community Forum](https://community.passbolt.com/t/meet-sakura-and-layette/14919). 

## More resource types in Quick Access

Passbolt 5.18 expands Quick Access support to Secure Notes and Custom Fields, allowing users to access all their resources directly from Quick Access. Users can quickly search, preview, and copy these resources without opening the full Passbolt application. 

Both resource types seamlessly integrate with Offline Mode, ensuring they remain accessible even when disconnected from the server. Additionally, Quick Access automatically suggests relevant Notes and Custom fields for a website if the URL matches. 

## Additional Improvements

This release brings autofill improvements to enhance reliability on high-resolution displays and refines recognition logic on login forms to ensure smooth auto-filling. Also, large sharing operations are now more than twice as fast, speeding up access updates when sharing 200 or more resources at once.

## Maintenance and Security

Passbolt 5.18 strengthens the Duo second factor. Duo now confirms that the account completing it belongs to the user signing in, so a compromised first factor can no longer be paired with a different Duo account. The check is on by default when enabling Duo for the organization for the first time. On existing ones it stays off until an administrator enables it, so align each user's Duo identifier with their Passbolt email first to avoid locking anyone out.

A detailed security bulletin will follow with more information about the security issues addressed in this release. In addition, routine dependency upgrades have been completed to keep the application fast and secure.

## Conclusion

Many thanks to everyone who provided feedback, reported bugs and contributed to making Passbolt better.

## 🏎️ Performance Improvements

## Faster dependency discovery in large repositories

`run --all`, and `find` or `list` with `--dependencies`, are faster in large repositories, including ones with no `dependency` blocks. The time spent linking units to their dependencies now grows linearly with the number of units instead of quadratically.

In [benchmarks](https://github.com/gruntwork-io/terragrunt/blob/main/internal/discovery/benchmark_relationship_test.go) on an AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395, discovering units and their dependencies in a generated repository of 10-unit dependency chains:

| units | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10 | 0.63ms | 0.63ms |
| 100 | 5.2ms | 5.0ms |
| 1,000 | 56ms | 47ms |
| 10,000 | 1.32s | 443ms |

At 10,000 units, memory allocated during discovery dropped from 8.6 GB to 1.9 GB.

## Faster discovery with dependent filters

Terragrunt wastes less time resolving symlinks in discovery. Dependent filters, such as `--filter '...vpc'` were able to reduce the number of wasted syscalls to resolve symlinks, improving dependent discovery.

On a repository of 1,024 units, discovery with a dependent filter took 30% less time from the repository root and 47% less time from the target unit's directory on an M3 Max. It also allocated 12-16% less memory.

## Faster discovery of dependencies

Discovery prepared to read a `terragrunt.stack.hcl` in every directory named by a `dependency` or `dependencies` block, even when the directory was a unit. It now does that work only when the stack file exists.

In [benchmarks](https://github.com/gruntwork-io/terragrunt/blob/main/internal/discovery/benchmark_dependents_test.go) on an AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395, selecting the dependents of a unit that every other unit depends on, run from that unit's directory:

| units | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10 | 2.9ms | 2.3ms |
| 100 | 118ms | 86ms |
| 1,000 | 11.1s | 8.0s |

At 1,000 units, memory allocated during discovery dropped from 26.7 GiB to 10.3 GiB.

## 💡 Tips Added

## `inputs-read-not-tracked` — Points at files read in `inputs` that reading filters miss

Terragrunt does not track a file read in `inputs`. A unit with this configuration is not selected by `--filter 'reading=config.yml'` or by a Git filter when `config.yml` changes:

```hcl
# terragrunt.hcl

inputs = {
  message = yamldecode(file("config.yml")).message
}
```

The same applies to `inputs` in an `autoinclude` block of a stack file.

Commands that track reads, such as `run --all` with a reading or Git filter and `find --reading`, now print the `inputs-read-not-tracked` tip pointing at each such read:

```text
TIP (inputs-read-not-tracked): Terragrunt does not track files read in `inputs`, so reading and Git filters miss the units and stacks that read them.

Untracked file read in `inputs`
 --> app/terragrunt.hcl:4:24
  |
4 |   message = yamldecode(file("config.yml")).message
  |                        ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ Read the file in `locals` and reference the local here.

Untracked file read in an `autoinclude` block's `inputs`
 --> live/terragrunt.stack.hcl:16:29
   |
16 |       policy = templatefile("policy.json.tftpl", { role_arn = dependency.iam.outputs.role_arn })
   |                             ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
   |
   = Mark the template as read with `mark_as_read` in the stack's `locals`, then pass the local as the path here.

See https://docs.terragrunt.com/features/filter/attributes#reading-based-expressions
```

See [Reading-Based Expressions](https://docs.terragrunt.com/features/filter/attributes#reading-based-expressions). Suppress the tip with `--no-tip inputs-read-not-tracked` or `--no-tips`.

## 🔒 Strict Controls Added

## `cas-source-inside-stack` strict control

A `unit` or `stack` block with `update_source_with_cas` could set a source inside the directory of its own stack file, e.g. a catalog with its stack at the root and its units under `units/`:

```hcl
# catalog/terragrunt.stack.hcl

unit "foo" {
  source                 = "./units/foo"
  update_source_with_cas = true
  path                   = "foo"
}
```

Stack generation copies the stack directory whole. For a `stack "bar"` block with `source = "../catalog"`, the generated stack contained the unit twice, and `run --all` ran both, the copy without the values its stack gives the generated unit:

```text
.terragrunt-stack/bar/.terragrunt-stack/foo
.terragrunt-stack/bar/units/foo
```

Existing support will be retained for v1.x for backwards compatibility, to obey the [Terragrunt 1.0 guarantees](https://docs.terragrunt.com/process/1-0-guarantees#hcl-configurations).

Terragrunt now warns about each such block:

```
WARN  Setting the source of a `unit` or `stack` block with `update_source_with_cas` to a directory inside the stack directory is deprecated and will be removed in a future version of Terragrunt. Stack generation copies the stack directory whole, so `run --all` also runs the copy. Move the source out of the stack directory, and select the stack with a `//` subdirectory in its source.
WARN  stack bar: unit "foo" in terragrunt.stack.hcl sets update_source_with_cas on source "./units/foo" inside the stack directory, so the generated stack also contains a copy of it; move the source out of the stack directory and select the stack with a // subdirectory in its source
```

With the new [`cas-source-inside-stack`](https://docs.terragrunt.com/reference/strict-controls/active#cas-source-inside-stack) strict control enabled, each of those blocks is an error instead:

```bash
terragrunt stack generate --strict-control cas-source-inside-stack
```

Move the stack into a subdirectory of the catalog, e.g. `stacks/bar`, keep its sources outside that subdirectory, and select it with `source = "../catalog//stacks/bar"`. The `cas-source-inside-stack` control is also part of the `deprecated-configs` group.

- Fix chance of skipped components in nested bundle stacks on first run of `terramate generate`.
- Fix multiselect inputs with `prompt.options` not accepting an empty selection in `terramate ui`.

This security release fixes server environment disclosure through JqAgent and bypasses of the enforced outbound proxy.  Upgrade installations that enable JqAgent or rely on `OUTBOUND_PROXY` to restrict users' outbound requests.

## Security fixes

- JqAgent now starts jq with an empty environment.  User filters can no longer read server environment variables through `env` or `$ENV`.  This affects installations with jq support enabled through `USE_JQ`.  [GHSA-3f56-748g-q34j](https://github.com/huginn/huginn/security/advisories/GHSA-3f56-748g-q34j)
- Enforce `OUTBOUND_PROXY` for HTTParty, open-uri and directly built Net::HTTP connections, including JiraAgent and WeiboPublishAgent.  These paths previously bypassed the configured proxy, allowing users to reach destinations it was intended to block.  The fix also covers related paths in StubhubAgent and default Scenario imports.  [GHSA-98rv-h5p4-9rgr](https://github.com/huginn/huginn/security/advisories/GHSA-98rv-h5p4-9rgr)

Thanks to [@akash111-hue](https://github.com/akash111-hue) for reporting both issues.

## Upgrade notes

No database migration is required for these fixes.  Update to `v2026.11.09` and restart Huginn's processes, or pull and recreate containers using the official release images.

If `USE_JQ` was enabled while untrusted users had accounts, treat secrets supplied through Huginn's environment as potentially exposed.  Rotate `APP_SECRET_TOKEN` and any affected database, SMTP, OAuth or other credentials.  Rotating `APP_SECRET_TOKEN` invalidates existing sessions.

JqAgent filters using `env` or `$ENV` now receive an empty object.  Pass intended inputs through the Agent's `variables` option instead.

Requests that previously bypassed `OUTBOUND_PROXY` may now fail under its destination policy.  Use an `http://` proxy URL for compatibility with open-uri clients; HTTPS destinations still use a CONNECT tunnel.  Normal routing is preserved when `OUTBOUND_PROXY` is unset.  See the [upgrade guide](https://github.com/huginn/huginn/blob/v2026.11.09/UPGRADING.md#jqagent-environment-isolation-and-outbound-proxy-enforcement) and [outbound request configuration](https://github.com/huginn/huginn/blob/v2026.11.09/doc/manual/outbound-requests.md).

This release also refreshes Ruby dependencies.

> ⚠️ **Authentication changes in Rocket.Chat 9.0.0**
>
> LDAP, SAML, and Custom OAuth now require a premium plan, and Drupal, Facebook, LinkedIn, Meteor, X (formerly Twitter), WordPress, and Dolphin logins are removed. Community workspaces that use any of these must upgrade their plan or move users to a supported login method before updating, or those users won't be able to log in.
>
> **Supported on every plan, including Community**
>
> - Local login (username or email and password)
> - Google, GitHub, GitLab, Apple, and Nextcloud
>
> **Premium plans only (Starter, Commercial, Government, and Defense)**
>
> - LDAP, SAML, and Custom OAuth
>
> Eligible organizations with up to 50 users can switch to the free Starter plan.
>
> **Before you update:** make sure at least one administrator can log in with a local username and password.
>
> Preparation steps and how to recover access: [Prepare for Authentication Changes in 9.0.0](https://docs.rocket.chat/docs/prepare-for-authentication-changes-in-9-0-0)

## Summary

### Security and Compliance
_Security improvements, authentication changes, data protection, and vulnerability fixes._

MCP clients can sign in with OAuth access tokens, and private **TURN servers** for voice calls reach only users on a call. Workspace-wide ABAC enforcement adds required room attributes, ABAC-managed channels and teams, and attribute editing with a membership preview. LDAP, SAML, and custom OAuth now require a Premium license. Several built-in OAuth providers, Atlassian Crowd, anonymous write, the `query` and `fields` parameters, and the `/ufs` path are removed. Fixes cover SSRF checks for Livechat triggers, NoSQL injection, message and UiKit validation, federation checks, role permissions, 2FA email limits, and dependency updates.

### Messaging and Collaboration
_Features and fixes related to messaging, channels, discussions, and communication workflows._

Native video conference calls, powered by LiveKit, and a native XMPP server for federation are now available. Admins can control user status under **Manage** > **Workspace** > **Status and presence**. The user card and **Full profile** panel are redesigned, AI search gains filters, and the composer adds list buttons and Emoji 17.0. New workspaces start with Omnichannel turned off. Fixes improve message rendering, unread indicators, emoji sizing, client memory use, keyboard navigation, screen reader support, voice calls, and Livechat transcripts.

### Platform and Extensibility
_Developer platform, APIs, integrations, and application framework improvements._

Apps gain new UiKit blocks and elements, including `header`, `markdown`, `table`, and `video` blocks and a date-time picker. The Rocket.Chat JavaScript DDP SDK is now the official realtime SDK. REST API status codes now return 401 without a session and 403 for refused requests, and 157 deprecated DDP methods are removed. `channels.invite` accepts `userIds` and `usernames`, and the `POST /v1/push.token` response is flattened. Fixes tighten pagination and DM creation.

### Data, Storage, and Infrastructure
_Database, performance, storage, and system-level improvements._

The official Docker images move to Node.js 24.22.1 on Debian bookworm. The upgrade drops unused MongoDB indexes, and the `MESSAGE_MAX_PARSE_LENGTH` default is now 10,000 characters. Fixes improve the retention policy on large rooms, realtime updates and memory use in microservices deployments, and outbound connections after errors.

### Admin, Configuration, and Workspace Management
_Administrative controls, configuration settings, and workspace management improvements._

Users can have multiple labeled phone numbers; the `phone` field becomes `phones`, and `freeSwitchExtension` becomes `sipExtension`. Meteor is removed from the web client, so custom scripts must use the REST API, and webhook scripts run without Babel. WebDAV, Gravatar, legacy federation and Matrix Bridge, legacy GCM push, and several unused settings are removed. Fixes improve LDAP connection tests and sync reporting, and the **Invite members** panel layout.

>For further details, check out the [release notes](https://docs.rocket.chat/docs/rocketchat-release-notes).

## Security fixes

### GHSA-773c-7fc3-342g - Open redirect on /external_redirect without a session
The external link page (`/external_redirect`) redirected visitors straight to any given URL when external link capture was disabled or not covered by an Enterprise token. No login was needed. A link on the domain of an OpenProject instance could therefore send visitors to any website, which could be used for phishing.

The page now always shows the "Leaving OpenProject" warning with the target address. Visitors have to confirm before they leave, whether or not external link capture is enabled.

This report has been responsibly disclosed by GitHub user [gputier](https://github.com/gputier) through GitHub advisories.

For more information, please see the [GitHub advisory #GHSA-773c-7fc3-342g](https://github.com/opf/openproject/security/advisories/GHSA-773c-7fc3-342g)

### GHSA-9c69-v342-vqr7 - Arbitrary zero-argument method invocation on visible projects via unvalidated attribute parameter in `InplaceEditFieldsController`
This release fixes a critical vulnerability (CVSS 3.1 score **9.4**) in the in-place editing endpoint for project attributes. Users who could view a project were able to trigger unintended operations on it, including deleting the project and its subprojects and reading information they were not permitted to see. On public instances, without required login, this was possible for anonymous users. All versions from 17.2.0 onward are affected. Outside of our usual policy to only release patches for the currently supported version, for this critical vulnerability we will be issuing patches for versions 17.9.7, 17.8.2, 17.7.3, 17.6.1 and 17.5.2. Installations running 17.2 to 17.4 should upgrade to one of these releases.

Thanks to GitHub user [ccsimplyspolit](https://github.com/ccsimplyspolit) for responsibly disclosing this issue.

For more information, please see the [GitHub advisory #GHSA-9c69-v342-vqr7](https://github.com/opf/openproject/security/advisories/GHSA-9c69-v342-vqr7)

### GHSA-g75c-9rjg-8cvj - Read-only repository members can push to Git repositories through a query string in the Smart HTTP URL
OpenProject decides if a Git Smart HTTP request is a read or a write by matching the request URI against a pattern for `git-receive-pack`. The pattern is anchored at the end of the URI and includes the query string. When a query string is added or the parameters are reordered, the request is treated as a read.

A project member with only the "Browse repository" permission can therefore push to a managed Git repository that is served through the Apache integration, although pushing requires the "Commit access" permission.

This report has been responsibly disclosed by GitHub user [OXWaidwerk](https://github.com/ChristianTeroerde) through GitHub advisories.

For more information, please see the [GitHub advisory #GHSA-g75c-9rjg-8cvj](https://github.com/opf/openproject/security/advisories/GHSA-g75c-9rjg-8cvj)

### GHSA-jwhj-v5mg-3f4f -  POST /api/v3/storages: a normal non-admin user reaches constantize.new because the admin check runs after the object is built
`POST /api/v3/storages` resolved the requested storage provider type with `constantize` before checking permissions. An authenticated non-admin user could make the server look up and instantiate arbitrary classes, but the request always ended in an error response for that user. No data was exposed or changed, and other users weren't affected. Provider types are now resolved against a fixed list of known storage providers.

The vulnerability was responsibly disclosed by GitHub user [0xVijay](https://github.com/0xVijay) via GitHub security advisories.

For more information, please see the [GitHub advisory #GHSA-jwhj-v5mg-3f4f](https://github.com/opf/openproject/security/advisories/GHSA-jwhj-v5mg-3f4f)

### GHSA-pggp-67cq-xgrg - Arbitrary zero-argument method invocation on visible projects and work packages via attribute macros in exports and emails
Attribute macros (`workPackageValue:…` / `projectValue:…`) in rich text are resolved on the server when the text is exported or sent by email. The attribute name in the macro is not validated and is used as a method name on the referenced record. A user who can write rich text can therefore make the server call arbitrary public zero-argument methods on any work package or project visible to the user who exports the text or receives the email. This allows deleting records (e.g. `destroy`) as well as reading data that is not exposed otherwise (e.g. `attributes`).

Found internally by the OpenProject team during a code audit following GHSA-9c69-v342-vqr7.

For more information, please see the [GitHub advisory #GHSA-pggp-67cq-xgrg](https://github.com/opf/openproject/security/advisories/GHSA-pggp-67cq-xgrg)

### GHSA-pv79-v2hf-5gg8 - Anonymous password change endpoint has no per-account limit and works on normal accounts
This report has been responsibly disclosed by GitHub user gputier through GitHub advisories.

For more information, please see the [GitHub advisory #GHSA-pv79-v2hf-5gg8](https://github.com/opf/openproject/security/advisories/GHSA-pv79-v2hf-5gg8)

# 3.3.17

3.3.17 is a security release. It caps the length of author display names, which any visitor could set to almost 1 MB, and fixes `.etherpad` imports into pads created through the HTTP API. Upgrade as soon as you can.

### Security

- **Pads — author display names are now type-checked and capped at 128 characters ([GHSA-w4w9-j4c3-hjf6](https://github.com/ether/etherpad/security/advisories/GHSA-w4w9-j4c3-hjf6), #8475).** The name sent in `CLIENT_READY` and `USERINFO_UPDATE` was stored with no type or length check, so a visitor with no account could save a name of nearly 1 MB, bounded only by the socket's message size. That name was then sent to everyone who opened the pad. A name that wasn't a string also broke the admin author search. Names must now be strings and are trimmed and cut to 128 characters, with any Unicode accepted. Names already stored are capped when read back, so oversized records are no longer rebroadcast. The pad's name fields enforce the same limit. Reported by @MAYASEVEN.

### Notable fixes

- **Import — `.etherpad` files import again into pads created through the HTTP API (#8470).** Since 3.3.13 (#8420), importing a `.etherpad` file from the import dialog failed with a permission error when the target pad was created by `createPad`, `createGroupPad`, admin create-pad or ep_post_data, and the file came from a pad a browser created. When the importer isn't the target pad's creator, the file's first author is now rewritten to that creator. Text keeps its original authorship. An importer still can't make themselves the creator, and pad settings still come from the target pad.

### Other changes

- Localisation updates from translatewiki.net.
- Dependency updates.

This release contains the following fixes: 

- Fix team and account deletion infinite spinner [#2436](https://github.com/cryptpad/cryptpad/pull/2436)
- Fix team mailbox not archived when the team is deleted
- Fix static files can't be shared with teams [#2434](https://github.com/cryptpad/cryptpad/issues/2434)
- Fix invalid CSP errors in Firefox browser console
- Fix possible parse error on the server
- Fix filenames of log files produced by the eviction scripts
- Fix eviction scripts stopping too early

## Incompatible changes

* **Phishing**: URL mismatches are now scored separately from phishing. Rewrite permissions come from dynamic maps, and selected security URL wrapper hosts are trusted. The mismatch rollout is kept conservative
* **Symbol options**: options are stored verbatim. `[]{};,` and `%` are percent-encoded only when options are joined (X-Spamd-Result, X-Virus, metadata_exporter, ClickHouse, the symbols log line). asn, reputation, rbl, dmarc, content rules and MULTIPLE_UNIQUE_HEADERS now insert multi-value results as separate options
* **SPF**: a record is evaluated in the order of its terms, and the qualifier of an include or redirect is applied after the mechanisms. Before this, `-ip4:1.2.3.4 +ip4:1.2.3.0/24 -all` let 1.2.3.4 pass
* **DKIM**: signatures with duplicated tags or l=0 over a body are rejected. So are RSA keys under 1024 bits and keys that are not of the type k= declares. The d= domain is lowercased in results, symbol options and glob maps
* **SMTPUTF8 addresses**: ASCII syntax violations now score as INVALID_FROM_ASCII_ADDR and INVALID_RCPT_ASCII_ADDR (1.0). INVALID_FROM_8BIT and INVALID_RCPT_8BIT fire only for 8-bit addresses
* **MIME and archives**: a multipart child without Content-Type is read as text unless its data is binary, so short-text fuzzy hashes of such children change. get_files(n) and get_files_full(n) count files rather than names, and other names of an entry are flagged as aliases. With no limit given, archive.unpack is capped at 1 GiB of output and a million headers, and it uses only the filters libarchive implements itself
* **Lua API**: lua_util inflate returns errors as a second value. lua_url get_redirected is no longer an alias of get_phished. The image flag is set only on urls seen solely as image sources, so get_urls returns a link that is also an image source. A get_date result of 0 means no date in the time('message') selector and the spamassassin plugin, so DATE_IN_PAST rules no longer match mail without a Date header
* **PDF**: content streams are read as operands and operators, pages follow the page tree in document order, and words are spaced by text position moves. Extracted text changes as a result

* **SMTPUTF8**: address checks per draft-ietf-mailmaint-smtputf8-syntax
* **Phishing**: explicit rewrite trust maps
* **New rules**: BAD_DKIM_SIGNER (multimap) matches every checked DKIM d= against the bad_dkim_signers glob map. HTML_TINY_PIXEL_TRACKER and the HTML_TINY_PIXEL_PROBE composite catch contentless messages with tiny external tracking pixels. DATE_FAR_FUTURE_NO_TZ flags far-future Date headers without a timezone
* **Truncated and unreadable content**: new symbols report content that was cut short or could not be read:
  * MIME_UNREADABLE_ARCHIVE, MIME_TRUNCATED_ARCHIVE and TEXT_WORDS_TRUNCATED
  * OOXML_INCOMPLETE and SVG_INCOMPLETE

* **Deeper inspection**: EXE_IN_ARCHIVE checks names in archives named as documents, in OOXML/ODF packages and in the first 1000 names. The HTML tags limit is harder to reach, and hidden elements are tracked past it

## Bug fixes

* **Critical**: a header line without a colon in one unauthenticated HTTP request aborted the worker, and so did an empty Deliver-To header. An empty MIME part stopped parsing, so no part after it was scanned
* **Milter and proxy**: fixed session use-after-frees on upstream failure and on a second end of body. Also fixed:
  * reads past CONNECT and MACRO commands
  * transaction handling on MAIL and on a repeated CONNECT
  * QUIT handling behind queued output, and writes after a partial write
  * references to ESMTP arguments
  * sockets of keepalive backends that were never closed
* **HTTP and protocol**: the lua_http error handler no longer runs on freed data after a reply. Idle connections are pooled by TLS verification and peer address and checked for pending data. A plaintext reply to an encrypted request is refused. forbid_local also blocks unspecified, shared, reserved, multicast, unique local, link-local and IPv4-in-IPv6 addresses. X-Rspamd-Rcpt-Esmtp-Args keeps keywords without a value and bounds recipient indexes, and repeated From, IP and Settings-ID headers no longer leak
* **Redis**: RESP3 maps, sets and doubles no longer crash the worker. The pool no longer frees a held connection that was closed, hashes key fields with their lengths, fails on AUTH/SELECT errors and caps connections per server. TLS options now reach script uploads, statistics_dump and fuzzy storage. Sentinel supports TLS and credentials and keeps the last valid upstreams after discovery errors. fuzzy_storage keeps the order of updates to a repeated digest
* **DNS and maps**: librdns takes only the records that answer the question and now retries truncated replies over TCP. IDN names are converted without the transitional rules, and lua_dns PTR requests are fixed. Maps back off retries by failure class: a map whose first fetch failed used to stay empty for 100 minutes. Maps also honour Retry-After: 0 and keep polling after connect or DNS failures
* **SPF and DMARC**: SPF fixes:
  * macro and prefix-length parsing, dual prefixes (`a/24//64`) and `ip6=`
  * macros and ptr now use the checked address
  * flattened records are bounded, and `rspamadm dnstool spf-flatten` follows the record order

### New
- Log files in `logs/` now rotate when they reach 10 MB: `grav.log` becomes `grav.log.1`, older copies are gzipped (`grav.log.2.gz` and on), and five are kept. `grav.log`, `security.log` and `scheduler.log` rotate as they are written, an hourly `log-rotate` scheduler job catches plugin logs, and `bin/grav logrotate` runs it by hand. Change or turn it off under `system.log.rotate` (Configuration → System → Error handler)
- A page can unpublish everything below it along with itself. Set `cascade_unpublish: true` on a page (Options → "Unpublish child pages too"), and while that page is unpublished, by `published: false` or by its `publish_date` / `unpublish_date`, every page below it is unpublished too: left out of menus, collections, the sitemap and search, and not served. The pages below keep their own `published` setting, so they are back as they were once the parent is published again, and a section given a `publish_date` goes live all at once. `system.pages.cascade_unpublish` (Configuration → System → Content) sets the default for every page, and is off. `$page->unpublishedBy()` returns the route of the page that hides a page

### Bugfix
- A backup profile's Scheduled Backup switch now decides on its own whether the backup runs. An old Enabled or Disabled entry for the backup job in `user/config/scheduler.yaml`, which classic admin wrote whenever its Scheduler page was saved, used to override it, so backups could stop with the switch on [#4397](https://github.com/getgrav/grav/issues/4397)
- A scheduler job that fails now keeps what it printed to standard output as well as its error output, so the reason shows in the job's history, `user/data/scheduler/status.yaml` and the output file. Most console commands print their errors to standard output, so a failed run used to be recorded with no output at all
- A page with a link or image whose address is longer than any file path, such as an inline image written as `/data:image/png;base64,...`, no longer turns into an error page on servers with `open_basedir` set
- Several Grav sites on one server no longer try to load each other's files. The class loader's APCu cache is now kept separate for each site, so a class found in one site's `vendor/` folder is never looked up at another site's path [#4392](https://github.com/getgrav/grav/issues/4392)
- The Page IDs option and the GFM and table Markdown options in Configuration → System use translation keys instead of English written into the blueprint, so they can be translated. The English comes from Admin2 2.2.13 and Admin 1.10.63

## 5.62.0 (2026-11-12)

### :warning: Security Warning and Notice :warning:

Strapi was made aware of a vulnerability that was patched in this release, for now we are going to delay the detailed disclosure of the exact details on how to exploit it and how it was patched to give time for users to upgrade before we do public disclosure.

### ⚠️ Changes to be aware of

#### Invalid boolean filter values now return 400

Filtering a boolean field by an empty value, `yes`/`no`/`on`/`off`, a value padded with spaces, or a number other than `0`/`1` now returns a 400 error. Before, most of these silently matched the `true` entries. `TRUE`/`FALSE` (and `T`/`F`) are now read case-insensitively, and routes that query the database directly answer invalid filter values with 400 instead of 500.

([#28172](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/pull/28172))

#### Optional time in date-time list filters

In the Content Manager list view and the audit logs, date-time filters now accept a date alone, which matches that whole day. You can still add a time, which matches that exact minute. Plugins that use the admin `Filters` component with a date-time option should pass their filters through the new `toApiFilters(filters, options)` before calling their API.

([#28367](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/pull/28367))

#### Faster, safer email validation

Email validation no longer slows down sharply on crafted input, which could stall the server from the unauthenticated forgot-password routes. The stricter pattern also rejects a dot inside a domain label, such as `example.co..uk`.

([#28059](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/pull/28059))

#### Upload Content API ignores unsupported query parameters (since 5.61.1)

`GET /api/upload/files`, `/api/upload/files/page` and `/api/upload/files/:id` now pass only supported query parameters to the upload service. Projects with `api.rest.strictParams` enabled get a 400 for unknown parameters, as on other Content API routes. Other projects keep ignoring them.

([f531775c87](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/commit/f531775c87))

#### Data transfer: `--throttle` now applies to entities and links

`strapi export`, `import` and `transfer` now apply `--throttle` and global transforms to every stage. Before, they skipped entities and links. If you run a transfer inside Jest (`export`, `import` or `transfer` called from a test), start Node with `--experimental-vm-modules`. The CLI commands do not need it.

([#28206](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/pull/28206))

#### Upload `File` type now requires five keys (TypeScript only)

`width`, `height`, `formats`, `previewUrl` and `provider_metadata` are now required on the `File` type of `@strapi/upload`, though their values can still be `null`. TypeScript code that builds a `File` object itself, such as a test stub or a mock provider, must set them, for example to `null`.

([#28209](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/pull/28209))

#### Policy handlers may be async (TypeScript only)

`Core.PolicyHandler` can now return a promise, and `policyContext.state` is typed. TypeScript code that uses a policy handler's result directly must `await` it.

([#28469](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/pull/28469))

#### Sanitizer and traversal results use `unknown` values (TypeScript only)

`traverseEntity`, `defaultSanitizeOutput`, `sanitizePasswords`, `Sanitizer` and `Validator` from `@strapi/utils` now take and return objects with `unknown` values, `id` included. Check a field's type before you use it (for example `typeof value === 'string'`). In strict-mode projects, type the entity parameter of a custom sanitizer or validator as `Record<string, unknown>`.

([#28539](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/pull/28539))

# v2.22.7: Translation Module Stable, Cross Module Joins, Promotion Events

The Translation Module is out of beta and is available in all Medusa installations by default, and cross-module joins replace the Index Module as the default mechanism for filtering across module boundaries.

CMS_BREAK -->

## Highlights

### Translation Module Stable

The Translation Module is out of beta is now installed in all Medusa projects by default. You can use translation features to translate content for products, categories, custom data models, and more.

Learn more in the [Translation Module documentation](https://docs.medusajs.com/resources/commerce-modules/translation).

---

### Cross-Module Joins Replace the Index Module

Medusa now resolves cross-module queries using direct database joins rather than the Index Module, including in the `/store/products` API route. The Index Module is deprecated and will be removed in a future release.

If you have explicitly registered the Index Module in your project, you can remove it from your `modules` configuration. Cross-module queries via `query.graph()` and API filters that span module boundaries continue to work without any changes.

```ts
// In medusa-config.ts, remove the Index Module registration if present:
// { resolve: "@medusajs/index" }
```

Learn more about [cross-module joins with Query in the documentation](https://docs.medusajs.com/learn/fundamentals/query#filter-by-linked-data-models-property).

---

### Security Fix for Index Module

This release also comes with a security fix for users that have enabled the Index Module feature flag in their store. It ensures proper handling of `?` characters in query parameters passed to the `/store/products` and `/store/product-variants`.

If you can't update to this version, we urge you to download and apply the patch of your Medusa version:

---

### Promotion and Campaign Events

Medusa now emits events when promotions, promotion rules, and campaigns are created, updated, or deleted. Subscribers can react to these events to trigger automation workflows in response to discount and promotion changes.

[#17136](https://github.com/medusajs/medusa/pull/17136)

---

### Medusa Cloud Plugin

A new Medusa Cloud plugin integrates the admin dashboard with Medusa Cloud, surfacing in-app announcements about platform updates and new features directly in the admin UI. The plugin is included automatically for projects deployed on Medusa Cloud.

[#17518](https://github.com/medusajs/medusa/pull/17518)
