# Spree 6.0.4

Spree 6.0.4 is a patch release with a refreshed admin dashboard and seller panel, a richer seller page for marketplace operators, and built-in diagnostics for bug reports. It also fixes a set of checkout completion races, draft order totals, and email lookups in apps that encrypt emails.

```bash
npx spree upgrade
```

---

## ✨ New features

- **Diagnostics and Send feedback.** Settings → System info shows an anonymised report of versions, runtime, infrastructure, changed settings and recent errors, and Send feedback in the account menu opens a bug report with it attached. Developers get View as JSON with Copy as curl on detail pages and a request inspector (Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+D). [#15176](https://github.com/spree/spree/pull/15176)
- **Seller page for operators.** The admin seller page shows the last 30 days of sales and commission, orders still to fulfill and products in review, with the seller's products and orders as full lists. Every section edits in place, including the returns address and holiday mode. [#15177](https://github.com/spree/spree/pull/15177)
- **Approve sellers without onboarding.** Operators can approve a pending or invited seller directly, for example a seller they set up on a vendor's behalf, by overriding the requirements. [#15187](https://github.com/spree/spree/pull/15187)
- **Team invitations for active sellers.** Operators can add people to the team of a seller that is already approved. [#15170](https://github.com/spree/spree/pull/15170)
- **Seller panel settings.** Sellers get Settings → General (contact details, addresses, holiday mode), Profile (what shoppers see) and Taxes, each as one simple form page. The Complete profile step no longer requires a contact email unless the operator turns that on. [#15190](https://github.com/spree/spree/pull/15190) [#15191](https://github.com/spree/spree/pull/15191)
- **Stock adjustment reasons.** Bulk stock updates can carry a reason such as received, damaged or count, shown in the stock history. [#15138](https://github.com/spree/spree/pull/15138)
- **Category and collection events.** Adding a product to, or removing it from, a category or collection publishes an event that webhooks can subscribe to. [#15104](https://github.com/spree/spree/pull/15104) by @KacperMekarski

## 🧭 Admin dashboard improvements

- **A refreshed look.** The admin dashboard and seller panel use the Inter font, a neutral palette with a near-black dark theme, lighter list tables with a compact density option, and order pages organised into sections. [#15136](https://github.com/spree/spree/pull/15136)
- **Media library.** A large media dialog with search, filters, upload, grid or list view and sorting, a full-screen media editor, and images picked per variant. Sellers can remove images from their products. [#15136](https://github.com/spree/spree/pull/15136)
- **New pages and pickers.** Supplier and customer group pages, one customer picker with Add new customer everywhere, adding company members from existing customers, own and seller tabs on stock locations, and out of stock and low stock filters across all locations. [#15136](https://github.com/spree/spree/pull/15136)
- **Settings pages.** Payments, storefront and store settings have their own pages, and the settings menu sits beside the main navigation. [#15136](https://github.com/spree/spree/pull/15136)
- **Missing price warning.** An active product warns when shoppers paying in a currency cannot see it because it has no price there. [#15165](https://github.com/spree/spree/pull/15165)
- **Table search option.** Lists that cannot search by free text no longer show a search box. [#15164](https://github.com/spree/spree/pull/15164) by @KacperMekarski

## 🐛 Bug fixes

- Removing a line from a draft order updates its totals and quantity. [#15179](https://github.com/spree/spree/pull/15179)
- Sign-in, staff invitations, order search and personal data export work in apps that encrypt customer emails. [#15123](https://github.com/spree/spree/pull/15123)
- A cart holding the last units in stock completes checkout instead of failing on its own reservation. [#15157](https://github.com/spree/spree/pull/15157) by @beobungbu
- A cart cannot be deleted or have items added while its checkout is completing. [#15147](https://github.com/spree/spree/pull/15147) by @beobungbu [#15169](https://github.com/spree/spree/pull/15169)
- A payment webhook that fails to settle an order retries instead of leaving a charged buyer without an order. [#15133](https://github.com/spree/spree/pull/15133)
- Store credit uses the order's own store payment method. [#15151](https://github.com/spree/spree/pull/15151) by @beobungbu
- Repeating a request with the same idempotency key but a different query is treated as a different request. [#15149](https://github.com/spree/spree/pull/15149) by @beobungbu

## ⬆️ Upgr

Vendure v3.8.2 is a patch release containing a batch of core, dashboard, CLI, `@vendure/create` and plugin fixes, including a fix for Dashboard extension pages which broke after a redeploy.

If you use `RedisCachePlugin`, cancel Orders from the `ArrangingAdditionalPayment` state, serve resized SVG assets, or script `vendure auth status` or `@vendure/create`, read **Behaviour Changes**.

## Core

- Recalculating an unchanged Order gives the same totals every time when an item-level Promotion depends on an order total condition such as `minimum_order_amount` (#5663, closes #5605). Before, the result could alternate between two values.
- `updatePromotion` checks that each action has its required condition, as `createPromotion` does (#5676, closes #5675). Before, an update could leave `buy_x_get_y_free` without its condition, and order price calculation then threw `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'freeItemsPerLine')`.
- An Order in `ArrangingAdditionalPayment` can only move to `Cancelled` once all of its lines are cancelled, as from every other state (#5672, closes #5671). Before, the check was skipped and allocated stock was not released.
- The default search index includes every variant passed to `updateVariantsById` and `updateVariants`, not only the first 50 (#5674, closes #5673). This showed when a Collection gained more than 50 variants at once: `search({ collectionId })` returned 50 of them.
- A Customer cannot change their email address to one which belongs to another Customer, including a guest Customer with no User (#5680, relates to #5640). The request returns `EmailAddressConflictError`. Before, two Customers could end up with the same address.
- `authenticate` returns `InvalidCredentialsError` for an empty input or a strategy with `null` data, instead of an internal error with no error code (#5622, closes #5621).
- `createAssets` with `translations` and no custom fields returns the translated Asset (#5713). Before, selecting `name` failed with "Cannot return null for non-nullable field Asset.name".
- Blocking event handlers:
  - A circular dependency between three or more handlers is reported with a `Circular dependency detected` error which names the handlers, instead of `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` (#5632, closes #5630). A handler whose registration was rejected no longer stays registered.
  - Two handlers which declare the same constraint from both sides (A is `after` B, and B is `before` A) are ordered instead of throwing a `RangeError` (#5665, closes #5664).
- `RedisCacheStrategy` removes expired entries from its tag sets and gives each tag set an expiry, so tag sets no longer grow without limit (#5683, closes #5682). The session cache tag gained one member per session. `invalidateTags` now works in batches of 1000 and throws on a command error instead of ignoring it.
- The polling job queue waits for a job which is being claimed before it stops (#5565, relates to #4949). Before, the application could close while the job was already marked `RUNNING`, and nothing settled it afterwards.
- A migration no longer de-duplicates translations in a table which the same migration creates, and logs de-duplication only when it removes rows (#5702). New projects no longer log "The … table does not exist. Skipping de-duplication." for every translation table.

## Dashboard

- Every build gives its JavaScript chunks new file names (#5772, closes #5564). Before, an extension chunk could keep its file name while the entry chunk it imports got a new one. Because `/assets` is cached as immutable, the browser then ran the old chunk, and extension pages showed "Not Found" or failed with `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'useContext')` after a redeploy.
- After logging out and signing in as another user, the Dashboard loads that user's settings (#5669). Before, the new user saw the previous user's settings, and their active Channel was saved into the new user's settings.
- Dashboard widgets keep the position given in `defaultSize.x` and `defaultSize.y` when the user has no saved layout and the position is free (#5658, closes #5616). The built-in widgets have new default positions.
- Expanded child Collections reload in the new language when you switch the content language (#5706, closes #5704).
- Changing a line's quantity in Modify order and on the draft order page works when the OrderLine has a relation custom field (#5697, closes #5696). The field was sent by its output name, which the API rejects.
- The asset picker's select button, the upload toasts and the move Collections dialog use proper plurals in every locale (#5590, relates to #5482).
- In `useExperimentalBundle` mode, styles match source mode (#5709). Before, selects could render too narrow and some `@vendure-io/ui` classes, such as the breadcrumb separator, were missing.

## CLI and @vendure/create

- `vendure console link` has a new `--console-project <id|slug>` option which selects the Console Project without the picker (#5685). With `--non-interactive` it creates the Project Link from the login stored by `vendure auth login`.

  **Minor changes**
  
  - `@verdaccio/config`, `@verdaccio/store`, `@verdaccio/tarball`, `@verdaccio/web`: Add the experimental `flags.tarballMetadata` option, which lets the web UI show the README of the exact version being viewed and fills missing `dist.fileCount`/`dist.unpackedSize` from the tarball itself. ([#6409](https://github.com/verdaccio/verdaccio/pull/6409))
  
    The npm registry does not always include READMEs in package metadata: for some large packages (for example `react`) the README field is empty for every version, and Verdaccio by default keeps only the latest README for locally published packages (`publish.keep_readmes`). The web UI then showed "No README data found" or the README of a different version.
  
    With the flag on, a tarball is only ever unpacked in two situations: in the background right after a version is published, and when the web UI asks for a README the manifest does not have, reading the cached tarball or fetching it from the uplink. Package installs never unpack tarballs, so install performance is unaffected. The README is kept in memory, and `dist.fileCount`/`dist.unpackedSize` are written into the cached manifest when the uplink did not provide them. At most two tarballs are read at a time, and duplicate requests share one read.
  
    Tarballs larger than `tarball_metadata.max_size_mb` (default 20) are never unpacked; those versions keep the previous fallback to the latest README. The flag is off by default and the option may change or be removed in a later prerelease:
  
    ```yaml
    flags:
      tarballMetadata: true
    tarball_metadata:
      max_size_mb: 20
    ```
  - `@verdaccio/middleware`, `@verdaccio/proxy`, `@verdaccio/store`, `@verdaccio/ui-theme`, `@verdaccio/web`: Show the provenance and registry signature of a version in the web UI. ([#6447](https://github.com/verdaccio/verdaccio/pull/6447))
  
    The package sidebar gets a "Provenance" section, under "Distribution", when the selected version carries a sigstore attestation or a registry signature, the fields registry.npmjs.org attaches to every version it signs. Its chip reads "Provenance: SLSA v1" for a version with provenance and "Registry signature" for one that only has a signature. Clicking it opens a dialog with the statement type, the signing key ids and a link to the attestation bundle. Nothing is verified in the browser: the dialog states what the registry metadata contains, and verification remains the job of `npm audit signatures`.
  
    The dialog also shows what the provenance statement says about the build, read from the attestation bundle by a new web endpoint, `GET /-/verdaccio/data/package/provenance/<name>?v=<version>`: the builder (GitHub Actions, self-hosted or not, or GitLab CI/CD, the two environments npm and Yarn generate provenance in), the source repository, ref and commit, the workflow file or job, the build run and the Sigstore transparency log entry, each linked to its origin. The endpoint relays the bundle from the uplink the version was synced from, applies the package access rules and answers 404 for versions without attestations. The build details therefore need an uplink that serves the npm attestation endpoint, `/-/npm/v1/attestations/<name>@<version>`, as registry.npmjs.org does; a Verdaccio upstream will only do so once it gains the registry signature routes, which are a separate change, and against such upstreams the dialog shows the summary and the bundle link alone. The request is made only when the dialog opens and only when the server announces the endpoint through the new `capabilities.provenance` UI option, so the theme keeps working against older servers without a single failing request: the chip, the dialog summary and the bundle link come from the sidebar data alone, and the build details simply stay out.

With this `npm audit signatures` verifies registry signatures and provenance attestations of proxied packages exactly as it does against registry.npmjs.org. Enable it with:

    ```yaml
      signatures: true
    ```

## [1.185.0](https://github.com/semgrep/semgrep/releases/tag/v1.185.0) - 2026-11-10

### ### Added

- PHP: Improved virtual call resolution for basic trait composition. (CODE-9176)
- Supply Chain: a `requirements.txt` dependency declared as a version range (`litellm>=1.10`) or with no version (`flask`) now produces a finding for every advisory whose affected versions overlap the declared range, in both the Python and native resolvers. Such a finding has no single installed version to confirm, so it needs review. A range line next to a pinned copy of the same package produces no finding of its own, since the pinned copy names the installed version. (SC-4243)
- Secrets: emit structured, privacy-safe telemetry for custom validator HTTP requests (hostname, port, status, latency, rule/scan correlation) (SMS-3122)
- Set `SEMGREP_LOG_JSON_FILE` to emit structured execution events with scan metadata alongside existing text output. (SMS-3670)

### ### Changed

- Scans are slightly faster. The dataflow analyses build the name of each variable with a plain string join, and no longer with `Printf` and `Format`. On 6 open-source repos, the scan time was a median of 3% lower, with identical findings. (dataflow-variable-keys)
- The `semgrep/semgrep` Docker image no longer includes the OpenSSH server (`sshd`) or `sftp-server`. It now installs only the OpenSSH client (`ssh`, `scp`, `ssh-keyscan`, `ssh-agent`, `ssh-add` and `ssh-keygen`), which is all git needs to fetch over SSH. Container scanners will no longer report sshd-only CVEs against the image. (docker-ssh-client-only)
- go grammar update (v0.25.0):

  - Go source parsing now supports generic type aliases, preserving type parameters, constraints, and alias semantics. Existing alias patterns can match these declarations; spelling generic parameter lists in rule patterns remains unsupported.
  - Go correctly parses unnamed map parameters and results in mixed signatures such as ([]string, int, map[int]int, error), allowing function patterns to match those signatures.
  - Go correctly represents chained indexing such as table[key][next] as nested index expressions, restoring matches for nested-index patterns.

  (go-v0.25.0)
- julia grammar update (v0.25.0):

  - Julia source parsing and rule patterns now support public API declarations while distinguishing them from export declarations and calls named public.
  - Julia source parsing and rule patterns now support outer-qualified loop bindings, preserving their distinction from ordinary bindings and a variable named outer.
  - Julia parsing and matching now support typed const fields without initializers in mutable structs.
  - Julia source parsing and rule patterns now support renaming imported macros, such as import A: @m as @n and import A: @m as @B.n, and keep the @ on macro names in imports, exports, and public declarations.
  - Julia rules can now match unary ± expressions and distinguish binary ± from ∓, reducing operator-related false positives.
  - Julia numeral juxtaposition such as 1__2 is now represented as multiplication by __2 and can be found by multiplication patterns.
  - Julia function-definition patterns now retain where constraints, avoiding matches against definitions with a different constraint.

  (julia-v0.25.0)

### ### Fixed

- OCaml: taint analysis now follows data through expression statements and
  sequence expressions. For example, in `let x = (r := 1; source ()) in sink x`,
  the value of the sequence is the result of `source ()`, so the finding on
  `sink x` is now reported. Taint also no longer leaks from one `match` case
  into the next one. (ocaml-expression-statements)
- OCaml: the last expression of a function body is now treated as the function's result, so taint flows through calls. (ocaml-implicit-returns)
- Semgrep no longer logs credentials embedded in a proxy URL (for example
  `HTTPS_PROXY=http://user:password@proxy:8080`) when it reports the configured
  proxy settings. (proxy-log-redact-userinfo)
- Logs and traces no longer include snippets of the scanned source code when a
  file fails to parse. Parsing exceptions now report the file, line, column, and
  the length of the unexpected text instead. Dependency resolution errors for
  malformed lockfiles are reported the same way. (redact-source-in-telemetry)
- On Windows, Semgrep now runs programs it calls by name, such as git and pysemgrep, only from fully qualified PATH directories. Previously Windows checked the current directory first, so an executable committed to a scanned repository could run during a scan. Initially reported by Aikido Security. (CODE-10122)
- pro: Reduced peak memory for large projects (CODE-10136)
- Supply Chain: the yarn v1 lockfile parser no longer reports a package named
  "dependencies" with an empty version when a blank line precedes the
  dependencies block of an entry, and it now keeps that entry's dependency
  edges. Entries without a version line are reported as parser errors instead
  of dependencies with an empty version. (SC-4214)
- Gradle module attribution now works for modules whose logical project name
  does not match their directory (a renamed `include` or a remapped
  `projectDir` in settings.gradle). The resolver's init script reports each
  project's actual build file, and dependencies are attributed to that file
  instead of falling back to the root manifest. (SC-4327)
- semgrep ci --no-suppress-errors with --allow-local-builds: when dependency resolution fails and the scan exits with code 2, the reason is now also in the `errors` of the JSON output (one entry per resolver error or lockfile parse error of each failed subproject, or a generic entry if none was reported; resolver errors include the failed command and the end of its output, with common credential shapes such as URL credentials and Authorization headers redacted), not only in the log. Previously the JSON had no error, so pipelines that read it could not tell why the scan failed. (SC-4348)

What's new in Pylint 4.1.4?
---------------------------
Release date: 2026-11-14


False Positives Fixed
---------------------

- Fix a false positive for ``using-constant-test`` when testing a method or function
  whose decorator is unknown or is a class, such as a third-party ``cached_property``.
  astroid still infers such a method as a method, but the decorator may have turned
  it into any other value.

  Closes #3484

- Avoid ``dict-init-mutate`` when an assignment's key or value references the dictionary being initialized.
  Stop the suggested dictionary literal before later assignments that reference the dictionary.

  Closes #7997

- Fixed a false positive for ``unreachable`` when a terminating function call
  (such as ``sys.exit()``) is inside a compound expression within a lambda body.

  Closes #8567

- Fix a false positive for ``used-before-assignment`` when a class body uses a module-level or builtin name that a method or nested class defined later in the same class body shadows.

  Closes #9134

- Fixed a false positive ``undefined-variable`` (E0602) when a name annotated
  without a value (``x: int``) is assigned with the walrus operator (``:=``) in
  the condition of a comprehension spanning several lines, and used in its element.

  Closes #11647

- Fix a false positive for ``method-hidden`` when a decorated method is inferred
  as a property.

  Refs #11732

- Fix false positives for ``bad-dunder-name`` on ``__prepare__``, ``__mro_entries__``,
  ``__buffer__``, ``__release_buffer__`` (Python 3.12+) and ``__replace__`` (Python 3.13+).

  Closes #11791



Other Bug Fixes
---------------

- Pyreverse now reports a clear error instead of a traceback when ``--class`` names
  an unknown class or module, or omits the module name when analyzing multiple modules.
  Targets whose inferred values are all known not to be classes are also rejected.
  If a target has several inferred values, Pyreverse uses the first class among them.

  Closes #22

- Fix a crash when linting a package whose parent directory is an implicit namespace package
  that also exists in ``site-packages`` or the standard library: the module paths of the files inside it could not be
  resolved, and the given package was reported without its package prefix.

  Closes #10278

- Fix a crash in the logging checker when a logging call uses a ``bytes`` format string that is not valid UTF-8.

  Closes #10813

- Fixed an ``AssertionError`` crash in the typecheck checker when accessing an attribute on an ``Enum`` exception instance.

  Closes #11638

- Fixed a crash in ``use-maxsplit-arg`` (``C0207``) when a ``str.split()`` or
  ``str.rsplit()`` call indexed by a variable is used inside a loop that assigns
  to a subscript, an attribute or an unpacked tuple (for example ``obj[0] = 1``,
  ``obj.attr = 1`` or ``a, b = 1, 2``). Such targets have no ``name`` attribute
  and previously raised ``AttributeError``.

  The index variable is now also recognized as changed in the loop when it is
  reassigned through tuple unpacking or an assignment expression (``:=``), which
  removes a false positive.

  Refs #11676

- ``--generate-toml-config`` and ``--generate-rcfile`` now include the plugins given with
  ``--load-plugins`` or ``--enable-all-extensions``.

  Closes #11699

- Checkers loaded with ``--load-plugins`` or ``init-hook`` are no longer registered twice in every
  worker process, which used to emit each of their messages twice when ``--jobs`` was greater than 1.

  Closes #11701



Other Changes
-------------

- Backslashes in message and option descriptions are now escaped in the generated
  documentation and in ``--full-documentation``, so ``use "\b" instead`` no longer
  renders as ``use "b" instead``.

  Closes #10737

- further CPE to more precise package identifier mappings [PR [#3886](https://github.com/anchore/grype/pull/3886) @westonsteimel]

## Upgrade notes

### Recheck browser received-data thresholds [#6496](https://github.com/grafana/k6/pull/6496)

`browser_data_received` now uses the encoded transfer size reported by Chrome DevTools when a response finishes, including responses in a redirect chain. This can differ from the previously computed response size, particularly for compressed responses. Recheck thresholds and baselines that use this metric when upgrading from an earlier version.

### Conversion changes for extension authors [#6629](https://github.com/grafana/k6/pull/6629)

Extension authors should check code that relies on Sobek's Go-to-JavaScript value conversion. Nil slices now become null/undefined instead of empty arrays, and `Runtime.ToValue()` dereferences only one pointer level. Use a non-nil empty slice when an extension API should return an empty JavaScript array. This guidance concerns extension implementations; k6 preserves empty-array results for the affected built-in browser, HTML, and gRPC APIs.

## Deprecations

### InfluxDB and Prometheus remote-write outputs [#6665](https://github.com/grafana/k6/pull/6665)

The built-in `influxdb` and `experimental-prometheus-rw` metrics outputs are deprecated and planned for removal in k6 v3. They continue to work in v2.4.0 but now log a deprecation warning when used. We recommend migrating to the `opentelemetry` metrics output.

## New features

### Trace the test execution hierarchy [#6605](https://github.com/grafana/k6/pull/6605)

The experimental `native-tracing` feature adds spans for the test run, each scenario, each VU activation, and each iteration. Browser spans become children of the corresponding iteration, so you can follow browser activity within the wider test execution.

Enable the feature and configure an OpenTelemetry traces output:

```shell
k6 run --features=native-tracing --traces-output=otel=http://localhost:4318 script.js
```

The hierarchy is `k6.run` → `scenario` → `vu` → `iteration`. Spans include scenario and execution identifiers. Failed iterations record errors, while iterations interrupted by the end of a scenario are marked as interrupted. The feature is opt-in and requires an enabled traces output.

### Sign and exchange keys with Ed25519 and X25519 [#6525](https://github.com/grafana/k6/pull/6525)

WebCrypto now supports Ed25519 signing and verification, and X25519 key agreement. Both algorithms support key generation and import/export, including JWK keys.

For example, generate an Ed25519 key pair, sign a message, and verify its signature:

```js
export default async function () {
  const keys = await crypto.subtle.generateKey('Ed25519', true, ['sign', 'verify']);
  const message = new Uint8Array([104, 101, 108, 108, 111]);
  const signature = await crypto.subtle.sign('Ed25519', keys.privateKey, message);
  const valid = await crypto.subtle.verify('Ed25519', keys.publicKey, signature, message);
  console.log(valid); // true
}
```

Thanks, @BlairCurrey!

### Hide credential headers in debug logs [#6607](https://github.com/grafana/k6/pull/6607)

Use `--http-debug-redact` with `--http-debug` to mask credential headers in HTTP requests and responses, and in gRPC metadata:

```shell
k6 run --http-debug --http-debug-redact script.js
```

Redaction covers `Authorization`, `Proxy-Authorization`, `Cookie`, `Set-Cookie`, `X-API-Key`, `X-Auth-Token`, and `X-Amz-Security-Token`. Authentication schemes, cookie names, and cookie attributes remain visible to help with debugging. You can also enable it through `K6_HTTP_DEBUG_REDACT` or the `httpDebugRedact` script option.

Redaction is disabled by default. It only masks these headers and metadata keys; URL query parameters and bodies logged with `--http-debug=full` remain unchanged. Thanks, @digitalcrab!

### Inspect structured gRPC error details [#5711](https://github.com/grafana/k6/pull/5711)

gRPC responses now expose structured error details from `grpc-status-details-bin` through `response.error.details`. This lets scripts inspect field-validation errors, retry information, and other details supplied by a server instead of relying only on an error message.

k6 resolves both standard Google error-detail types and custom types loaded through the client. If details cannot be converted, the error still includes its code and message. See [the gRPC error-details example](../examples/grpc_error_details.js) for a complete script. Thanks, @yordis!

### Send HTTP QUERY requests [#6481](https://github.com/grafana/k6/pull/6481)

The new `http.query(url, body, params)` convenience method sends an HTTP `QUERY` request. It accepts a request body and the same request parameters as the other HTTP convenience methods.

```js
import http from 'k6/http';

export default function () {
  http.query('https://example.com/search', JSON.stringify({ term: 'k6' }), {
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  });
}
```

Thanks, @ashrafiucse!

With this release, Terminal 1.25 is being rolled out to General Availability; see [the prior version](https://github.com/microsoft/terminal/releases/tag/v1.25.2733.0) for overall release notes.

## Changes

* (1.26 backport) conhost: we now always use the "cls" detector to prevent screen clearing from committing the entire (virtualized) text buffer (#19957)

## Bug Fixes
 
### Accessibility
 
* The "delete" confirmation flyouts will no longer be truncated on higher Text Scaling settings (#20868)
 
### Terminal Emulation

* The Kitty Keyboard Protocol mode will now be maintained properly across main/alternate screen buffer switches (#20768)
* `LNM` line feed mode will no longer be mishandled when it is toggled before and after a newline in the same packet (#20863)
* Applications can no longer set window titles longer than 1000 characters (like xterm) (#20839)
* Applications which scroll the screen buffer will once again be translated properly (such as `vi` from 1996) (#20774)
* Clicking on a URL while an application is reading mouse reports will no longer generate a spurious mouse release event (#20756) (thanks @OmarMashal0!) (edit: er, I (@DHowett) cannot confirm that this is actually fixed)
* Injected keyboard input will no longer come out with unexpected vkey values such as `0xFFFF` (#20800) (thanks @shrikargs7-cloud!)
* Terminal once again sends the `ENHANCED_KEY` state to console applications for Alt and F7 (#20619) (thanks @TheJesper!)
 
### Others

* `useAcrylicInTabRow` users rejoice! We've fixed one of the major sources of flickering in the title bar (#20881)
* `file:` URIs containing Unicode characters will no longer send us into a wild tailspin (#20809)
* Terminal will no longer load up a US keyboard on you (whoops) (#20769)
* Writing a non-numeric value in the command history pop-up will no longer act unexpectedly (#20779)

Changes since Git for Windows v2.56.0(4) (October 26th 2026)

This addresses the security issues CVE-2026-111760, CVE-2026-113408, CVE-2026-114466, CVE-2026-114467, CVE-2026-114469 and CVE-2026-105437.

### Security bug fixes

* [CVE-2026-111760](https://github.com/git/git/security/advisories/GHSA-vp2w-7xxj-jvxr):

  Recursive clones are susceptible to Remote Code Execution: an attacker-controlled repository can be crafted in a way that exploits a bug in Git whereby Git can be fooled into overwriting a gitfile (used for submodules) with a symbolic link that then points to a directory with malicious config or hooks. The config or hooks may have attacker-specified code.

* [CVE-2026-113408](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/git/-/work_items/809):

  It is possible for a server to advertise an unborn HEAD that contains path-traversal characters (e.g., `refs/heads/../../../TARGET`). With the files ref backend that can lead to ref-updating actions to write to unwanted files.

* [CVE-2026-114467](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/git/-/work_items/810):

  When Git strips the GPG signatures from a commit message, it only accounts for two signatures. A commit message containing more than two signatures therefore causes a stack memory corruption.

  This can be triggered when using `git merge` with a tag which contains more than two signatures. As such, this makes way for a DoS attack which can potentially also affect forges when such a tag is pushed to a remote and a merge action is initiated.

* [CVE-2026-114469](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/git/-/work_items/811):

  Git rejects patches larger than ~1 GiB, because its patch application code does not work well with large files. That check, however, only considered the size of the patch as it appears in the input, which for binary patches is much smaller than the size of the file the patch describes, as binary patches are compressed and encoded. A binary patch that inflates to a very large size therefore slipped past the check and crashed Git with an out-of-bounds read.

* [CVE-2026-105437](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/git/-/work_items/814):

  When merging, Git computes the size of the buffer holding the merge result in a way that can overflow for very large merges, which can be triggered by a large number of conflicts combined with a large `conflict-marker-size`. The resulting buffer can then be too small, and Git writes past its end (and, before and after that, before its start), corrupting the heap.

* [CVE-2026-114466](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/git/-/work_items/812):

  In response to CVE-2019-1348, `fast-import` disallows the `export-marks` feature by default. The features `rewrite-submodules-to` and `rewrite-submodules-from` as well as the option `export-pack-edges` that were introduced in the meantime also allow reading from arbitrary paths, and are therefore now also disallowed by default.

### New Features

* Comes with [Git v2.56.1](https://github.com/git/git/blob/v2.56.1/Documentation/RelNotes/2.56.1.adoc).

This release includes a major addition in Zellij: Zellij is now also a desktop terminal. To run it: `zellij terminal`. It works on linux, mac and windows.

**Nothing changes for the normal multiplexer** - Zellij can still run inside another terminal. Both sessions are the same and can be shared.

Packagers, please see: https://github.com/zellij-org/zellij/blob/main/docs/PACKAGING_DESKTOP.md

For a walkthrough of the new features, please see: http://zellij.dev/news/terminal-inbox-session-previews/

Note: The musl builds do not include the Zellij terminal, please use the gnu builds instead if you want access to it.

Please see the CHANGELOG for full details including some breaking changes for plugin developers: https://github.com/zellij-org/zellij/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md

## Ripple Preview

[Ripple Preview](https://ollama.com/library/ripple-preview) from Ricursive Intelligence is a 65B dense model built for agentic coding.

```sh
ollama run ripple-preview
```

## What's Changed

- Qwen3.8 Flash Next uses about 27 GiB less memory on Apple silicon
- `ollama launch claude` always routes Claude Code to the selected model
- `ollama launch` explains when a cloud model has been retired
- `/v1/responses` respects `truncation` and no longer silently truncates by default
- `/v1/models` returns an empty list instead of `null` when no models are installed
- CUDA 13.5 support for Windows on ARM
- Updated llama.cpp

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ollama/ollama/compare/v0.40.15...v0.40.16

### Added

- 🦾 **Agents in automations.** The automation editor now lets you choose a terminal and working folder, then select a coding agent available there. Scheduled runs use that saved terminal and folder, and check that the terminal and agent are still available before starting. Agent automations send their results to a chat; channel destinations remain available for ordinary models. [Commit](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/commit/21fc016141c73a0e11b428c61bde20527bbc228a)
- 📂 **Change terminal and folder during a chat.** You can now choose a different terminal or working folder after sending messages, including in temporary chats. Both controls remain disabled while a reply is being generated. [Commit](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/commit/a518ff1630b74ed6edd62538c5da4bb26cc6dd20)
- 🇧🇷 **Brazilian Portuguese translations.** Added missing translations for terminal and folder controls, Git actions, spreadsheet editing, voice notes, tab shortcuts, notification sounds and tool settings. Updated the explanations for document retrieval, tool permissions and voice settings. [#33945](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/pull/33945)

### Fixed

- 📂 **Files tabs follow terminal changes.** Switching a chat to another terminal now updates its open Files tabs to show that terminal's files, instead of leaving the previous terminal's folders on screen. With a terminal set to "Per chat", the Files tab also switches to the chat's own files after the first message. [#33954](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/pull/33954)
- 🧭 **Agents in unsupported model pickers.** Connecting a terminal no longer adds its coding agents to Admin Models, base-model selectors, Arena candidates, task-model settings, group defaults, sub-agent settings, channel mentions or the Playground. Notes also stop choosing a terminal agent for title generation. Agents cannot be saved or imported as custom models or their base models, and their chat menu no longer offers Edit. [Commit](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/commit/21fc016141c73a0e11b428c61bde20527bbc228a), [Commit](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/commit/6d3123b5b4a90962bff44c69c7e0bae0c65557d5)
- 🔌 **Agent list after switching terminals.** Changing terminals immediately removes the previous terminal's agents from the chat's model list while the new list loads. A model-list request from a chat you have left can no longer replace the current list. [Commit](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/commit/21fc016141c73a0e11b428c61bde20527bbc228a)
- 📋 **Copy buttons over plain HTTP.** At a plain HTTP address on your local network, copying comment links, search links, shared-chat links, webhook URLs, chat IDs, Git branch names, commit hashes and spreadsheet cells now works. Copy Formatted Text preserves formatting, and copied text keeps its final line break. [#33939](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/pull/33939)
- 📝 **Clipboard prompts and Auto-Copy Response over plain HTTP.** Prompts using the clipboard placeholder now insert into chats and channels even when the browser blocks clipboard access, with a message explaining that the clipboard could not be read. Auto-Copy Response stays off and shows a permission message instead of silently failing to turn on; turning it off no longer requires clipboard access. [#33939](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/pull/33939)
- 🧠 **DeepSeek thinking mode with skills, knowledge and memories.** These chats no longer fail with a missing reasoning error when the connection's Provider is set to "llama.cpp". DeepSeek thinking mode still requires that setting; connections using "Default" are unchanged. [#33950](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/pull/33950)
- 🏷️ **Labels on grouped tool calls.** With Tool Call Labels enabled, a group of tool calls keeps the labels that are present even if one call has none. The unlabeled call shows its tool name instead of making the whole group lose its labels. [#33932](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/pull/33932)
- 💬 **Tool labels in later replies.** The model now sees the labels it wrote for earlier tool calls when continuing a reply or answering another message, removing a reason it could stop writing labels as the conversation continued. [#33953](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/pull/33953)
- 🔎 **Knowledge searches containing punctuation.** Searches in knowledge files now find text such as "Art. 40" when the model marks the period as literal punctuation, instead of returning no matches. [#33936](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/pull/33936)
- 🪟 **Side Chat with Temporary Chat disabled.** Leaving Enforce Temporary Chat switched on while disabling Temporary Chat no longer prevents users from sending and saving side chats or dragging an existing chat into the side panel. [#33930](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/pull/33930)
- 🏠 **Home folder tab title.** A Files tab at the connected machine's home directory now says "Home" instead of showing the directory name, including when reopening saved tabs. Other folders keep their names. [Commit](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/commit/241c8c0e47e19b0adeb13d577ca538d2252b0ad4)
- 🦙 **Missing Ollama in Docker images.** Building the image that includes Ollama now fails if Ollama was not installed, instead of producing an image that cannot start Ollama after its download failed. [#33944](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/pull/33944)
- 📄 **Errors after leaving a chat.** Closing or leaving a chat while its tab layout is being saved no longer fills the server log with an error report for the dropped connection. [#33929](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/pull/33929)
